Breaking: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated

📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1056 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes.
  • But as Americans vote in the US midterm elections, it's time to think about how disgust shapes our politics, or whether our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?
  • The smell of rotten food can make us recoil.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes.

But as Americans vote in the US midterm elections, it's time to think about how disgust shapes our politics, or whether our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

The smell of rotten food can make us recoil. Certain sexual practices can provoke a similar reaction. And in today's polarized political climate, even political opponents can become objects of disgust.

Psychologists have long investigated whether sensitivity to disgust helps explain political beliefs. A review of 24 studies found that people who reported being more easily disgusted tended to hold more socially conservative views.

One explanation begins with evolution.

"We think that it evolved in part to reduce exposure to things that could make you sick," psychologist Yoel Inbar, of the University of British Columbia in Canada, told DW.

According to recent reports, but disgust is not a single emotion. The Three-Domain Disgust Scale, developed in 2009, distinguishes three types:.

One theory is that people who are especially wary of germs and disease may also prefer traditional social rules.

Inbar explains that avoiding potential sources of infection can also mean missing out on latest experiences.

"Some people are more on the cautious conservative side, and some people are more on the exploring risk-taking side when it comes to pathogen exposure," he noted.

It has been revealed that indeed, the language of contamination also appears in political rhetoric. During his 2024 presidential campaign, Donald Trump repeatedly described immigrants as "poisoning the blood of our country." Trump has also described himself as a "germaphobe.".

Inbar acknowledges that the evidence linking sensitivity to disgust with conservative political beliefs remains uncertain.

"We have hypotheses. I don't know that we have as strong of evidence as I would like," Inbar noted.

Industry observers note that disgust is not exclusively conservative. And what people find revolting can depend on their values.

A 2020 study titled "Is Disgust a "Conservative" Emotion?" found that liberals and conservatives were disgusted by different things.

Conservatives, generally aligned with the Republicans in US politics, reported greater disgust at examples involving sexual behaviors and drug use, while liberals, generally aligned with the Democrats, reported greater disgust at animal abuse and environmental pollution.

However, when asked how easily disgusted they were in general, there was no clear difference across the political spectrum.

Some early studies suggested conservatives showed stronger physical reactions to frightening or disgusting images, measured partly through changes in sweating.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

But subsequent research, including a 2020 study by political psychologist Bert Bakker at the University of Amsterdam, struggled to reproduce those findings.

Studies based on questionnaires, however, have generally found that people with more conservative attitudes report being more easily disgusted.

"If bodily reactions don't differ across political groups, why do feelings?" Manos Tsakiris, of Royal Holloway and the Centre for the Politics of Feelings at the University of London, told DW.

Tsakiris and colleague Mariana von Mohr wondered whether the answer might lie in how people perceive and interpret signals from their bodies.

Scientists call the perception of internal sensations, such as hunger, breathing or a racing heart, "interoception." It's sometimes called our eighth sense, alongside the familiar five, plus our senses of balance and body position.

"A bodily signal doesn't arrive with a label attached," Tsakiris told DW. "We have to notice it and make sense of it.".

The researchers surveyed 632 US adults, asking how much they noticed and trusted signals from their bodies — a measure known as "interoceptive sensibility.".

They found that people who were more easily disgusted by sexual behavior tended to be more conservative, regardless of how aware they felt of their bodies.

But for moral disgust, the link to conservatism was found only among people who reported lower bodily awareness.

What particularly surprised Tsakiris was that perceived bodily awareness alone had no link to political views.

"People who are highly attuned to their bodies were neither more liberal nor more conservative," he mentioned.

Inbar questions whether all forms of disgust are equally useful for studying political attitudes.

He and Joshua Tybur, one of the creators of the Three-Domain Disgust Scale, generally prefer measuring pathogen disgust — reactions to potential sources of disease — rather than sexual disgust.

Questions about sexual disgust may already reflect conservative beliefs about sex.

"It's almost asking people the same thing twice," Inbar remarked.

The fresh study found no significant link between pathogen disgust and conservative views.

In a recent development, inbar wants the findings on bodily awareness and disgust tested again, with predictions set out in advance. For now, he considers them "suggestive at best.".

Tsakiris suggests that people who struggle to understand their bodily feelings may be more vulnerable to political messages telling them what those feelings mean.

"I know what you're feeling. You're feeling angry or you're feeling disgusted about this thing," he said, illustrating how someone might put an emotional label on another person's unease.

Such labels could influence political behavior, he argues, although the study did not directly test this.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"This is how disgust can do political work: it can turn moral judgments about individuals into judgments about whole groups," he noted.

According to recent reports, the research cannot establish whether disgust shapes political beliefs or existing beliefs shape what people find disgusting. Bakker notes that political beliefs can influence how people describe their own personalities, suggesting the relationship could work both ways.

"Voting behavior is very complex and citizens make up their mind about politics in a complex way," he told DW.

In a recent development, inbar also cautions against exaggerating disgust's importance. "The thing to emphasize in your story is that the relationship, while it's consistent, is quite small," he said.

"It's one of the many influences on people's politics.".

Tsakiris advocates what he calls "critical feeling": questioning our emotional responses to provocative material, including social media posts, just as we question the information itself.

He also emphasizes discussing our feelings with others and listening to different perspectives, even when we disagree.

Sources indicate that "Life and politics and democracy is a contact sport," he said. Edited by: Rosalie Delaney.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool have performed much better since they were beaten by Fenerbahce in the Champions League a few weeks ago.

The Reds were torn apart by the Turkish Super Lig outfit with former Liverpool star Dirk Kuyt leading his team to a historic win.

Indeed, they are one of the better teams in Turkey but, compared to how much talent the Reds have among their ranks, they shouldn't have even had a chance to beat them.

That's why Liverpool's defeat was so hard to take for fans.

However, as mentioned, since then, things have gone well for Liverpool with the club even beating arch-rivals Manchester United 4-0.

Even though transfers are expected to occur in the January transfer window, Andoni Iraola still has a few players among his ranks who fans haven't seen the best of yet.

That's why Wednesday's Champions League tie against Club Brugge could be incredibly notable for one of them.

Victor Munoz has to start against Club Brugge.

Sunday's game was Liverpool's highlight of the season so far.

Their win against the Red Devils meant that they were thrusted back into fourth position and now find themselves seven points adrift of first-placed Arsenal.

This is still a decent gap to cut down but, it's a lot less daunting than the nine points that separated them over the international break.

During Sunday's victory against Man United, Victor Munoz was left on the bench to start with.

And, even though Liverpool were winning their arch-rivals 3-0 when the last 20 minutes of the game came upon them, Iraola still chose to bring the Spaniard on.

Most people expected that transfer to have been done to give those who started a rest but, Munoz had other intends.

In the 18 minutes of football that he played, his lightning quick speed and his ability to turn nothing chances into goals paid off as the 23-year-old bagged the Reds' fourth and last goal of the game.

He also maintained a 92 per cent pass accuracy and he even made one key pass.

This performance alone proves why he should be starting against Club Brugge in Liverpool's next Champions League tie.

Victor Munoz could become a key player for Liverpool in the next couple of years.

Munoz was Liverpool's bargain signing of the summer transfer window.

The Spaniard was brought in by the Reds for a fee worth around £35 million.

At the time, Newcastle were also trying to sign him but, in the end, he chose Liverpool.

Most fans thought that he'd be more of a back-up than anything else but, in reality, he's become a key member of Iraola's first-team squad.

His performances have been second to none and, even though he's often been used in his less preferred position of right-wing, he's still contributed to four goals in the 13 games he's featured in.

Here's hoping that, if Iraola does start the "outstanding" attacker on Wednesday, that he can put on another stellar performance.

#117748. Could AI give NFTs a second chance?

Could AI give NFTs a second chance?

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1056 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that remember the NFT boom of 2021?
  • What started as a marginal curiosity became a highly lucrative sector worth close to $40 billion (€36 billion) globally by the end of 2021, almost as valuable as the global art market itself.
  • Sources indicate that in the highly publicized bust that followed, many NFTs lost practically all their value.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that remember the NFT boom of 2021? The surge in trading of non-fungible tokens (NFTs), which are unique, blockchain-recorded digital assets, was one of the stranger economic offshoots of the COVID-19 pandemic.

What started as a marginal curiosity became a highly lucrative sector worth close to $40 billion (€36 billion) globally by the end of 2021, almost as valuable as the global art market itself.

Sources indicate that in the highly publicized bust that followed, many NFTs lost practically all their value. The wider cryptocurrency crash was particularly punishing for digital collectibles and largely, they have not recovered.

The sector is worth up to 97% less than it was at its height in January 2022, and sales continue to plummet. So far this year, total global sales of NFTs are less than $2 billion, according to FindWeb3, a cryptocurrency and blockchain jobs platform. That's more than 90% down from the peaks of 2021 and 2022.

Industry observers note that does that mean that NFTs will ultimately fade away to nothing, proving right those who dismissed them as a worthless fad? Or is there still some kind of future for them?

"NFTs will still exist, but it will be a niche collectible market," Ben Charoenwong, associate professor of finance at the business school INSEAD, mentioned. "This doesn't mean there cannot be booms here and there, but certainly not take off as people had imagined in the past.".

He thinks whatever future it can have will be "narrow" and indicates doubt is growing over the value of "non-fungible" as a concept. Non-fungible means an asset is unique and cannot be traded like for like, whereas fungible means it can be traded like for like, for example, with money.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

He notes that the recent trend of financial institutions converting real-world financial assets, such as bonds and stocks, into digital tokens recorded on a blockchain — the so-called tokenization boom — mostly relates to fungible assets.

However, Andrea Barbon, a finance professor at the University of St Gallen in Switzerland, thinks part of NFTs' future lies in this tokenization boom, as there are some examples of people trading unique real-world assets as NFTs.

According to recent reports, "NFT technology is really about ownership," he indicates. "They describe the ownership of a specific asset that could be a digital asset or real-world asset." He says things like real-estate contracts, expensive watches, artworks or luxury sports cars can now be tokenized, with NFTs created to represent these physical objects.

That immediately begs the question: Why would anyone want to have a digital, NFT version of their watch or sports car?

"Some people want to just speculate on the value of the physical asset and for them, it's great that you don't need to move the physical object around," Barbon said.

"If the object is a nice painting and you buy it from the US, you want to ship it to the UK, that's very costly, it's hassle and it's potentially not safe if the value of this painting is very high," he explained.

He states some companies, such as Courtyard.io, keep physical vaults to hold physical assets which are traded online as NFTs. He says very often, the owner has no interest in having physical possession of the asset.

Another area where he sees some promise for the future of NFTs is connected to artificial intelligence. He notes NFTs could help with AI safety, as they could be used to provide unique, verifiable, non-fungible identities for AI agents.

Ethereum and other blockchain providers are in the process of trying to build NFT systems that would represent and verify AI agents, something Barbon claims could be very successful.

He envisages a scenario where AI agents are recorded on an NFT blockchain and can then be identified and rated for safety and reliability.

In a recent development, "Everybody else can then see that the AI agent is actually doing well, you can trust it, it's safe," he says. "In order to do that, you need something which is uniquely attached to each AI agent and that can be an NFT.".

Another possible use he sees for NFTs in the AI era is that writers and artists could tokenize their work as NFTs so that if an AI agent ends up using it for training, the original work can be more easily identified as unique to the creator.

"Maybe you could then claim that the AI company has to pay you because they have used your content," Barbon says.

While the NFT craze of 2021 can now be seen as a classic bubble, many of those who invested in it have moved on to memecoins and other forms of fungible cryptocurrency, according to Ben Charoenwong.

"Overall, I think the market did not reject blockchains; it rejected non-fungibility," he says.

At the time of the craze, Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates mentioned NFT popularity was "100% based on the greater fool theory," the idea being that one can make money through the purchase of overvalued, fundamentally worthless assets as long as there is a"greater fool" willing to pay even more.

One of the most famous NFT collections was the Bored Ape Yacht Club, a series of drawings of apes in various locations in various states of boredom. "Obviously, expensive digital images of monkeys are going to improve the world immensely," Gates joked.

Industry observers note that in many ways, that collection's current status epitomizes NFTs' fall from grace better than anything else. Although it remains one of the biggest NFT marketplaces, its value has plunged.

In a recent development, the singer Justin Bieber bought one image for 500 ETH (Ethereum), or around $1.3 million dollars. The value fell by around 99% to around $14,000. He still owns it.

Yet the fact that these images still command such prices highlights they are not entirely worthless. That offers some hope to those who still believe in the technology. Alongside other possible applications linked to AI and tokenization, NFTs may still have a future, albeit a more modest one than when they first came to public attention.

By Darren Plant | 25 Nov 2026 10:10.

Southampton and Middlesbrough square off at St Mary's on Friday night in their first showdown since the conclusion of the Spygate saga.

While the visitors sit at the top of the Championship table, the Saints are just seven points adrift of opponents who are now viewed as one of their fierce rivals.

More than six months on from Tonda Eckert being found guilty of launching a spying mission on a Middlesbrough training session ahead of their playoff semi-final, Southampton have moved on from the controversy that rocked English football.

While Eckert will accept the attention that Friday's game attracts, he will remain focused on trying to secure promotion to the Premier League.

Despite being docked four points as part of their punishment from the Football Association, Southampton can move to within four points of Boro with victory on the South coast.

That said, the Saints have struggled for consistency of late, only collecting five points from four games and conceding a late equaliser to draw 1-1 at Sheffield United on Tuesday night.

Nevertheless, Southampton have been sensational at their home ground. Not only have 22 points being accumulated from a possible 24, they have scored 22 goals and conceded just five.

As for Middlesbrough, they make the long trip south having collected 12 points from eight fixtures, albeit only prevailing on three occasions.

Eight goals had been scored in back-to-back away successes at Stoke City and Bolton Wanderers, yet Kim Hellberg's side have failed to score in the last two such contests versus Wrexham and Watford.

However, 2-0 and 2-1 successes over Bristol City and Swansea City at the Riverside Stadium have ensured that Boro enter this game in top spot with 34 goals from their 17 matches.

Will Lankshear's return from a minor injury may also prove key. Despite being limited to a 62-minute outing versus Swansea, he netted his 14th Championship goal of the season.

Middlesbrough Championship form:.

Eckert will recall a number of his Southampton regulars for this contest, with Jack Stephens, Ryan Manning and Finn Azaz among those who will start.

James Bree may also feature on the back of his 30-minute outing versus Sheffield United after a minor injury, but Leo Scienza is likely to be named on the substitutes' bench at best after missing the last two matches.

Centre-back Keven Schlotterbeck will be sidelined until December through injury.

As for Boro, Sebastian Berhalter is expected to return in central midfield, with Myles Peart-Harris potentially being used further forward.

Providing that Lankshear shows no ill-effects from Tuesday's game, he should start, with David Strelec likely dropping down to the bench to accommodate an extra midfielder.

Despite concerns over an ankle injury, Neto Borges came through 90 minutes versus Swansea and seems in line to be selected at left-back.

Southampton possible starting lineup:.

Peretz; Roerslav, Abbott, Stephens, Manning; Downes, Ward-Prowse; Matsuki, Azaz, Dobbin; Larin.

Middlesbrough possible starting lineup:.

Vitek; Brittain, Phillips, Malanda, Borges; Morris, Berhalter; Cozier-Duberry, Peart-Harris, McGree; Lankshear.

It has been revealed that although Boro have returned from the November international break with back-to-back wins, we cannot ignore the intensity that these two teams will play at during this contest. That, and home advantage, may favour Southampton, leading us to predict a narrow victory for Eckert's side in a game that will include plenty of cautions.

Lewis Koumas has been a bit of a revelation for Liverpool.

The Welshman has joined up with the Reds' first-team squad thanks to the appointment of Andoni Iraola and his trust in youngsters.

When it was first revealed that Koumas would be staying with the Reds, most people thought he'd be the last option on the Spaniard's list.

However, he's somehow managed to become what looks to be his fourth or fifth-choice attacker.

Granted, most of his playing time has come as a striker but, he can also be used on either wing if needed.

But, with Hugo Ekitike returning and many different attackers now being linked with Liverpool, questions are being asked about what the future has in store for the 21-year-old.

Liverpool have added Gustavo Varela to their shortlist as a long-term target.

As mentioned, Koumas has been Isak's back-up so far this season.

The attacker has also been used in other positions but, when Ekitike is back in action, it's hard to see where and how the youngster is going to get a regular role.

That is, unless Ekitike comes back as a fraction of his former self, of course.

Obviously, Liverpool won't want that as they spent around £70 million on the Frenchman last term and, before his injury, he was probably their best player.

So, for Koumas, this season could be his last as a regular first-team option.

That is, especially after the latest transfer update from Football Insider on Liverpool's pursuit of Gustavo Varela.

"Liverpool will not prioritise a move to sign Monza striker Gustavo Varela in January, sources have told Football Insider," they wrote.

"The 21-year-old has emerged as a target for the Reds, having struck 11 goals from his opening 11 games in Serie A so far this term.

"The Reds are "keeping tabs" on the Portuguese youngster, with several top Italian clubs also having their "eyes fixed on him" at the moment.

"However, sources say that Varela is viewed as more of a long-term option at Anfield, and the club are not likely to make a move for him this winter.

"Monza are relaxed over their frontman's future for now, but they know that further interest from top clubs is inevitable if he continues to perform.".

If Liverpool sign Gustavo Varela, there is going to be no room for Lewis Koumas.

Obviously, keeping Koumas a part of Liverpool's looks is a massive thing for Iraola at the moment.

His endless running coupled with his keen eye for goal have made him an excellent option for Liverpool to have at their disposal.

However, with someone such as Varela, who is already the Serie A's top goal scorer at 21 years old, there's going to be a lot of competition ahead of him.

Indeed, his recent links with Liverpool are just rumours at the moment but, if he continues with this purple patch of form for the entire season, most clubs from across the world are going to be interested in acquiring his services.

Right now, it's unclear exactly what the Reds plan to do with their squad but, the fact that they're already trying to sort their shortlist out for the future means that they must have a pretty accurate idea about what they want to do.

Here's hoping that the Reds sign enough players to make a difference to their team and actually improve it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Janosch, the pen name of German author and illustrator Horst Eckert, won hearts around the world with his warm and simple sense of humor. He charmed children and adults alike with his iconic Tiger, Bear, Tiger-Duck and other animals.

Janosch created more than 150 books, which have been translated into over 30 languages.

In a recent development, his best-selling children's book, "Oh, wie schön ist Panama," translated into English as "The Trip to Panama," was so lucrative that Janosch was able to settle down on the Canary Island of Tenerife in 1980, where he lived together with his wife Ines. The writer and illustrator died peacefully at the age of 95, his publisher Bernhard Feil announced on Wednesday.

Industry observers note that janosch was born as Horst Eckert on March 11, 1931, in Hindenburg (now Zabrze, Poland) in what was then Upper Silesia. After World War II, his family had to flee to Germany.

In 1953, Janosch started studying at the Academy of Art in Munich, thinking that it would be easy to become an artist. He was however dismissed after just a few terms for "lack of talent.".

It has been revealed that but luckily for his later readers, Janosch did not give up. He continued to work as a freelance artist, soon discovering his second great gift, namely writing.

His first children's book about a horse named Valek was published in 1960.

Although Janosch became famous primarily for his children's books, he also wrote books for adults that focused on his own childhood.

Sources indicate that even though he wrote cheerful books for children, Janosch hardly had any positive memories of his own childhood, as his father was an alcoholic. He was beaten not only by him but also by his mother and grandmother. Raised in a strictly Catholic environment, he was continuously threatened to be punished by God.

Later on, Janosch tried to overcome the burden of his childhood memories by turning to alcohol as well.

He always expressed a great deal of understanding for children, trying to encourage them to stand up for their rights. As a result of his childhood experiences, Janosch did not want to have children himself, and his attitude towards the Catholic Church always remained divided. "As I am a sinner and a heretic, God will let me live a long life so that I can return to the Church," he told his biographer Angela Bajorek.

Recent findings suggest that janosch's animal figures are endearing but not always well-behaved. They love all kinds of nonsense. But even if they lie to each other or put their own interests first, the true winner at the end of stories is always friendship and solidarity.

Recent findings suggest that janosch achieved his major breakthrough with "The Trip to Panama," a story about two friends, a little tiger and a bear, who set out to find their paradise in Panama. After touring around in circles, they finally end up where they started out; they realize that their journey was the destination. Janosch received the German Youth Book Prize in 1979 for the work.

Recent findings suggest that janosch's protagonists have become familiar to generations of children all over the world. They come up over and over again in the various stories carefully illustrated with water colors.

Recent findings suggest that there is the honest lion Hans from the toy chest who fails to catch a nutcracker with his lies. There is Schnuddel and a ridiculous bragger Günter the Box-Frog. And then there is a tiger that collects mushrooms while looking out for his devoted friend, a bear, who always stands up for him even when the tiger temporarily leaves him because of a little pig in one of the stories.

Recent findings suggest that the "Tigerente," literally "Tiger-Duck," a wooden duck on wheels with yellow-brown stripes, appears on numerous pictures by the illustrator. At times, the animal has been tossed into a corner, at times it is hanging from the ceiling, or the Box-Frog pulls it across the drawing.

His iconic figures, especially the Tiger-Duck, have served as motifs on various items, from cups to stamps to jewelry, and even on airplanes. Film adaptations and TV series based on his stories were produced in German and English.

According to recent reports, guests who visited Janosch in Tenerife were impressed by his very modest lifestyle. He always remarked that hanging around in his hammock doing nothing was what he enjoyed most. And yet Janosch remained very active until the end of his life.

Industry observers note that from 2013 to 2019, he wrote a column for the German weekly Die Zeit, taking on the role of Mr. Wondrak, who commented on world affairs. Shortly before his 90th birthday in 2021, the complete collection of his Mr. Wondrak columns were published as a book in German.

Sources indicate that like the protagonists in his stories, Janosch always tried to content himself with few things. As he wrote in one of his books: "He who needs almost nothing, has everything.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 12:01 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 24 November 2026.

Given how rapidly things have unravelled under Sebastien Pocognoli, serious questions are now being asked of those in power at the Scottish Football Association.

Ian Maxwell and Craig Mulholland, the chief executive and chief football officer who led the recruitment process, certainly talked a good game when Pocognoli was appointed.

According to recent reports, however, when Mulholland took up his position in the summer, his remit was much broader than merely the appointment of a new head coach for the national team. He was tasked with trying to initiate a much-needed revamp of youth development throughout Scottish football.

Only a few months into the job, those plans have already hit the buffers due to resistance from clubs, despite the obvious need for more young Scottish players to play more first-team football.

The SFA had proposed including two Under-21 players starting in cup competitions and the same age group playing a minimum of 6 per cent of all available minutes across a season in league competition.

SFA chief football officer Craig Mulholland has met resistance in his bid to shake up the game.

When it immediately became clear that several clubs in Scotland weren’t keen on that, a newly introduced watered-down version was then put back on the table.

Now there have been reports that those intends might be booted even further into the long grass and possibly won’t even be voted on at all this season.

As is always the case, the self-serving interest from clubs in Scotland will always trump the need for national reform.

It has been revealed that but that is only part of the story. What is also of serious concern is the lack of quality coaching afforded to players in academies across the country.

If that was to be addressed, clubs would perhaps feel more obliged to play more younger players if they were ready for first-team football.

Industry observers note that it is a multi-faceted problem – and one which Mulholland is no closer to solving. Clubs are selfish and will serve their own needs, with no obligation to buy into any fresh proposals.

The SFA could stand firm and try to force some of these plans through as non-negotiable. A tough stance, albeit one that risks becoming messy.

Industry observers note that but nobody should be naïve enough to believe that self-interest from the clubs is the root of all problems here. It is much, much deeper than that.

There will be many more Champions League nights for Rio Ngumoha, although the 18-year-old will always remember this career landmark when his teenage skill plunged the opposition into fearful indecision and decided the game.

Recent findings suggest that this young man has not yet played 40 senior games but there is no doubting the quality. Alexis Mac Allister scored twice, Liverpool came from two goals behind, and it all ended with a panic that meant they came close to chucking it away again. But what everyone could agree on from this strange match of fluctuating fortunes was that Ngumoha looks like one of the best young players in Europe. He is also a bona fide two-sided winger, winning this game for Liverpool from the right wing rather than his conventional left-wing role.

Sources indicate that ngumoha created the second Liverpool goal for Ronald Araújo and then the third for Mac Allister with the game’s best moment. That was an electrifying run into a group of converging yellow shirts in which he beat two men and still retained the composure to pick out Mac Allister in the area. Even as the Argentine ran to the Kop to celebrate, that stand was chanting the name of the teenager from east London. Ngumoha was one of three academy boys in Andoni Iraola’s XI, along with Lewis Koumas and Trey Nyoni, and all had an impact.

Magic from Rio Ngumoha 🤩🪄 Alexis Mac Allister puts Liverpool ahead with his second goal of the night ⚽️ https://t.co/3FTNWOUYhl.

Iraola noted later that Ngumoha had taken care of the defensive work too against Sergi Cardona, an attacking left-back who scored his team’s second goal. From an attacking point of view, Iraola agreed, Ngumoha had periods of the game when he looked unstoppable. “If we can put Rio in situations one-v-one, he makes plays, [and] he produces things,” Iraola said. “The assist for Alexis is a lovely play. He could go down for a penalty but he decides to continue which is a great decision. Also endurance-wise he is able to play more minutes.”.

He becomes the youngest Liverpool player in Champions League history to register an assist in the competition. For Iraola it will be hard to leave Ngumoha out of the game against in-form Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday. “I believe in myself to do it,” Ngumoha said to Amazon Prime TV. “The more chances we get, the more it makes the opposition worry. I just keep going and be ruthless.”.

Iraola would later bring on the three £100m attackers whom he had left on the bench, with Sunday’s game in mind. Florian Wirtz, a half-time arrival, scored the fourth and Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak would later come on. Hard to call how it might go at home to Brighton. Liverpool’s defending was erratic at times, but their comeback was impressive.

It enabled Iraola’s players to deny Villarreal the space and possession they had enjoyed in the first half when they had taken a two-goal lead – chiefly because of the mistakes of the home team. However much that was destabilising for Liverpool, by half-time they were level.

Liverpool have a lot of work to still do on their squad.

Andoni Iraola took charge of the club just after they delivered an extremely shoddy title defence.

They ended up finishing fifth in the Premier League which resulted in them spending another £150 million on upcoming players.

And, while some of those transfers have worked out, it still feels like one or two, such as Bradley Barcola, still have a lot to live up to.

Obviously, as each season goes on, clubs try to add new players to their ranks and, since Liverpool's Premier League title rivals will be doing this, the Reds need to figure out ways to improve their ranks and get back to their best.

Unfortunately, for some of Liverpool's players, this means that their time at Anfield will need to be brought to an end.

Liverpool want to sign Abdellah Ouazane.

On Monday evening, Anfield Watch revealed that Liverpool are eyeing a move for Abdellah Ouazane.

The 17-year-old is right now plying his trade for Ajax in the Eredivisie and, despite being so young, he's already featured in 20 games for the Dutch outfit this term.

During those games, he's contributed to eight goals across all competitions and he has also been played in an array of positions.

The Moroccan was properly promoted to their first-team squad this term after Mika Godts accepted a move to PSG.

Indeed, Ouazane did feature for Ajax once in their domestic cup last season but, this term is the first where he's been a regular part of Miguel Ángel Sánchez Muñoz's team.

To make the deal even sweeter and even more likely, Ouazane is actually a Liverpool fan so, if the Reds went in for him, there's very little chance that he'd say no.

Abdellah Ouazane joining Liverpool would confirm Harvey Elliott's exit.

Right now, Liverpool don't really have a proper back-up for Florian Wirtz.

The young German has been the Reds' number 10 for most of the season with James McConnell taking over the role in some of Liverpool's cup games.

And, while McConnell has done a decent job, it's clear that the Reds need to start thinking about having a genuine back-up for Wirtz among their ranks.

Harvey Elliott was probably hoping that would be his role this term but, instead, he's been sent out on loan again.

His time with Valencia started off fairly poorly but, now, he's finally starting to find his feet with his main goal for the campaign likely to be get back on the good side of Iraola.

But, unfortunately for the Englishman, who was often one of the first names on Jurgen Klopp's team sheet, these recent links with Ouazane more or less confirm that his future lies away from Anfield.

That is, unless he can become Valencia's best player and start contributing to goals again.

The virtues of patience

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1334 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that it’s 13 December 2020.
  • Industry observers note that it was freezing and wet at the Emirates.
  • In a recent development, this was supposed to be fun.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Let’s take a journey back in time.

Sources indicate that it’s 13 December 2020. Arsenal versus Burnley.

Industry observers note that it was freezing and wet at the Emirates. Only 2,000 fans had been allowed in because of Covid, and my mum, my dad, my mate Ben and I made up four of them. We were socially distanced and wearing masks. My glasses kept steaming up.

In a recent development, this was supposed to be fun. Watching my team.

Willian was grotesquely slow. Alex Lacazette was profligate. Rob Holding was bald. Very bald. And Granit Xhaka was angry. So angry, in fact, that in the second half he put his hands around the throat of some opposition goon and, after a VAR review, got himself sent off. There were boos. As many as 2,000 people could muster, anyway.

Then our captain, Pierre Emerick-Aubameyang, headed a corner into his own net. You couldn’t make it up. Except you could. It was the only goal of the game.

Sources indicate that by then the steam fogging up my specs might as well have been coming out of my ears. In his player ratings, Andrew M called Xhaka the ‘King of the Idiots’ and described the match and the result as ‘utterly shit’. Which was fair.

It was our seventh defeat in 10 league games and our fourth in a row at home, something that hadn’t happened since 1953. We were 15th, five points above the relegation zone.

And who was top? Sp*rs. Managed by everyone’s favourite sociopath, Jose Mourinho. Having beaten us in the North London derby the week before, they couldn’t stop gloating.

I’d bought into the Arteta project hook, line and sinker. I still wanted him to be the right man for the job. I was just finding it harder to explain why I thought he was. The FA Cup win had been four months earlier. It felt like years.

The tree, to paraphrase our manager, was shaking.

It has been revealed that it had been shaking for a good two and a half years by then. The soggy bottom of the Arsene Wenger era had left its scars. Those two 3-0 defeats to City in the space of a week still make me wince. Then came the hope that Unai Emery might get us back on track. By the time we’d seen how that played out, I’d got into the habit of talking myself down whenever things looked up. Maybe we’ll get better. Give it time.

The trouble with rock bottom is you never know if there’s another floor below it. Was Burnley ours? I’m still writing about it six years later, so it was probably mine. There were games against Southampton and Everton before Christmas, and I can barely remember either of them.

Then came Boxing Day and a visit from Frank Lampard’s Chelsea. Is it reductive to say that was the day everything changed for Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal? Probably. But my word, watching Bukayo Saka, Emile Smith Rowe and Gabriel Martinelli tear about the place was the fix this addict needed. We went on an unbeaten run after that. Seven whole games! And for the first time in weeks, I was looking forward to what came next.

And here we are in November 2026. Reigning champions of England. Top of the league again. Five points clear. Odds-on favourites to retain the title after 10 games. Sure, throwing hundreds of millions of American dollars at the problem helped. But if there’s a lesson in all this, it’s that hard work and patience pay off.

Which is why I’m using today’s blog to appeal directly to Sir Jim Ratcliffe to give Michael Carrick a stay of execution.

Sources indicate that come on, man, you’re probably still paying off Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, maybe even Ralf Rangnick. Do you really want to go back to the drawing board all over again? Carrick is the man for the Manchester United hot seat. Just look at the way he wore a poppy-embroidered armband as well as a poppy badge at the weekend. The man doesn’t do half measures. He’s a two-scoops guy. Surely that’s something you, a multibillionaire British-born petrochemicals tycoon who lives in Monaco, can get on board with?

Industry observers note that I know Mauricio Pochettino might be tempting. He’s got floppy hair, a tan and, despite the Sp*rsy stench, has come to resemble a rather huggable teddy bear. But think it through, Jim. What if he comes in and everybody perks up? It’s much harder to make job cuts and to force out season ticket holders when people are enjoying themselves. Best get through that process first while Michael turns the oil tanker round. It’s not far off, promise, you’re on a two-game unbeaten streak!

Anyway, what would sacking Carrick say about patience? Look at Arteta. There were people who wanted him gone after Burnley and, as you’ve just read, I was close to joining them. Imagine if the club had listened to me. All those years of work, all that progress, all the joy I’ve had watching Arsenal lately. We could have thrown it all away because a man in a damp mask couldn’t see out of his glasses.

So give Carrick time. Give him January. Give him a full pre-season. And if things still haven’t picked up by this time next year, ask yourself whether one full pre-season, and £100 million on Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, was ever really enough.

I can only speak for myself, Jim, but I haven’t looked forward to watching Manchester United this much in years.

Right, let’s see if that works….

Recent findings suggest that the Interlull kicks into gear tonight. David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi are in action for Spain against Czechia, Riccardo Calafiori’s Italy take on France, and England face Croatia at Wembley.

Ezri Konsa and Myles Lewis-Skelly will both miss out at Wembley. Konsa is working on his fitness but will be available to face Spain on Sunday, while our Hale Ender is suspended after picking up two bookings in the Nations League.

In a recent development, elsewhere, ahead of Sweden’s game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, Viktor Gyokeres has been speaking to the press. Like Martin Zubimendi, he says he’s happy at Arsenal.

“I want to,” he remarked, when asked if he’s keen to stay at the Emirates.

Industry observers note that “It feels good when I’ve played. We’ve won most of the games. It was a tough loss in the cup (against Fleetwood). Otherwise it’s felt good for myself and the team, says the forward. I’ve been doing well lately when I’ve been playing. Right now it feels good.

Recent findings suggest that “The communication with (Mikel) Arteta is good. We talk about football and how we should play. Before a match, if I’m going to start, we talk about the opponents and what I should think about.”.

He was also asked whether the criticism he gets bothers him.

Sources indicate that “Sometimes it might get to me, but overall not so much. If I score goals and assists in the Champions League, I couldn’t care less what they say. It’s nice to do those kinds of performances. To deliver for myself and for the team. That’s where the focus lies.”.

According to recent reports, to be fair, I’ve not seen any serious chatter about selling Viktor in January. Whatever you think of him as a player, it would be a strange move unless we’re planning to spend serious money on the attack. And even then it would feel like an unnecessary risk given Kai isn’t exactly pulling up trees and latest faces will need an adaptation period.

If he’s happy keeping his head down and doing his bit for the team, I’d keep him around until the summer and reassess then.

It has been revealed that ok. I’m going to leave it there for today. All eyes on Old Trafford, I guess.

According to recent reports, as Gazzetta dello Sport writes, the Rossoneri are in a more-than-difficult position. Sitting 28th in the rankings, they are at the moment outside the qualification spots and calculations are difficult to make about how much they’ll need to improve.

It has been revealed that from the past two seasons, they’ll need between 14 and 16 points to qualify for the top eight, which feels like a distant hope. If they’re to achieve that amount, they must win all four of their remaining games and hope that 15 is enough.

Recent findings suggest that the play-offs, on the other hand, are more than feasible. Sitting four places off right now, there’s a one-point gap to overturn and history says they’ll need either nine or 10 points. This would allow far more room for error, with only two wins and a draw needed to ‘guarantee’ a spot in the next round.

In Greece, they’ll face the first hurdle and getting three points would make life much easier for everyone involved.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there was a lot of speculation as to how Arsenal might change this season having flung a 22-year-old monkey (how long do monkeys live for?!) from their back in May by finally winning a league title. Would lifting the Premier League trophy lead to a new era of more expressive, urbane football?

It has been revealed that I always had my doubts, not least because your style of play is always defined by your talent. Most of Arsenal’s elite talent is behind the ball. Arteta didn’t build Arsenal from the defence first, in my view, because he felt specifically that was the best way. It was just the area of the team that required the most attention when he was appointed.

Recent findings suggest that in attacking areas, he had talent, even if it wasn’t balanced. Aubameyang, Lacazette and Pepe with Saka and Martinelli coming to the boil was a good collection of talent, even if the pieces didn’t always fit neatly together. The list of defenders he inherited included Mustafi, Sokratis, Holding, Chambers, Kolasinac and Mari. That’s why he went defence first, broadly speaking.

It has been revealed that the moves the club have tried to make in recent seasons, especially this summer, shows you that Arteta wants his attack to be sharper than it is. For reasons I won’t relitigate here, the club were not able to add a number of high end attacking targets. Which means once again, Arsenal are reliant on Arteta’s coaching talents to squeeze more juice from the orange. Here are three things that have jumped out at me this season.

According to recent reports, arsenal spent a lot of money on Bruno Guimaraes this season and I will come onto some of the reasons why in the next section. But that signing has given Arteta a deep well of central options, with Rice, Bruno, Lewis Skelly, Odegaard, Merino and Zubimendi part of this midfield menagerie.

Arsenal use these options interchangeably and often according to game state. Art de Roche of the Athletic went into how Arteta has used the divergent profiles of Myles Lewis Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes so far in this campaign. In home games against Leeds and Everton, Lewis Skelly got the nod from the start.

In away games at Nottingham Forest and Liverpool, Bruno’s more robust approach was favoured. The pair have made significant impacts from the bench too. When the 1-0 victory at Anfield had become a little too ‘basketball’, Lewis Skelly came on and provided calm assurance in possession.

Recent findings suggest that when the Gunners needed a little more belligerence away at Sunderland, Bruno came on and larruped the ball into the top corner from 25 yards. However, Arteta didn’t part with a significant part of his summer budget for a 28-year-old (he turns 29 next week but, for now, he remains 28 because that’s how it works) to be a high level rotation option.

It has been revealed that against Hull City last weekend, Bruno was selected and he played deeper than Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard. As Adrian Clarke pointed out in his match analysis piece, Bruno passed the ball to Odegaard 25 times in that match and the pair exchanged 35 passes in total. The idea was clear, to use Bruno’s punchiness in possession a little lower to feed Odegaard.

Industry observers note that against Everton, Mikel Merino was selected in midfield and Lewis Skelly started at left-back. I think this was about more than mere rotation. Arteta always highly respects the aerial capabilities of David Moyes’ Everton team, which makes sense since he played in a David Moyes Everton team for such a long time.

In 2023-24, Arteta selected Fabio Vieira ahead of Kai Havertz in midfield at Goodison Park because he wanted to keep the ball on the floor (Arsenal won that game 1-0 via a short corner routine because they did not see the logic of aerial corners against a team like Everton).

Last season at the Hill Dickinson Arsenal enjoyed a season high for passes attempted and completed because they wanted to keep the ball on the floor and avoid transitions. Arteta has a carousel available to him in midfield and a different club in the bag depending on what is called for on the day.

Sources indicate that per Opta, Arsenal have been caught offside 35 times so far this season, at least 11 more times than any other team. That rate of 3.5 offsides per game is the highest of any Premier League team since 2009. Kai Havertz has been flagged 15 times now, the next highest offender in the league is Dominic Calvert-Lewin with eight. Opta provide a deeper dive on those numbers here.

In a recent development, so what does this tell us, aside from the fact that Havertz needs to work on his timing? It means that Arsenal are far more willing to go in behind and they are willing to test the opposition backline earlier in moves. This was a big part of the reason they signed Bruno in the first place, Arteta wants to play with the risk reward dial with the ball.

Havertz also hasn’t been quite good enough to finish some of those one v one situations when he has got in behind the opponent’s back line. He fluffed his lines against Hull last weekend and in the 3-0 defeat at Brighton, he blasted his effort straight at the Brighton keeper when put through one v one.

According to recent reports, but here, I will express my usual caveat, we need to normalise strikers missing chances and focus more on process than outcome. Most chances are missed, you want to worry when your striker is getting few shots. There have also been nascent signs that Arsenal have been using Gyokeres well in some of these situations.

Recent findings suggest that that Havertz chance at the Amex was created by Gyokeres taking one touch with his back to goal and hooking the ball past the committed defensive line. Gyokeres did much the same for Madueke in Prague. It seems like Arsenal have worked on getting Gyokeres to use his physicality to initially retain the ball- something he badly struggled with last season- but creating situations where he can release it quickly.

Arsenal’s out of possession prowess is one thing that has been a constant from last season. It is Arsenal’s superpower, so even when they can only manage one goal, it is usually enough to take maximum points. To retain their superpower, Arsenal changed to stay the same, if that makes sense.

It has been revealed that the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa was questioned by many but his presence has made the absence of a world class centre-back like William Saliba a sidebar, which is quite a feat. Arsenal ostensibly took William Saliba’s pizza chart and looked for the most Saliba like defender they could find and bought Konsa.

In a recent development, the loss of Saliba ought to have offered an enormous threat to Arsenal’s defensive stability. Arsenal’s tactical organisation out of possession is elite but so too are the individuals that helm it. Raya, Saliba, Gabriel and Rice are among the best players in the world in their respective positions.

Taking out one of those pillars ought to have derailed Arsenal’s defensive stability and it hasn’t because Konsa has the quality and poise to retain the team’s biggest strength. His pass completion stats are Saliba-esque and the quality of not giving the ball away needlessly is a significant part of the Gunners’ meanness.

How much Arsenal could improve in attack without significant additions was an unknown so Arteta could not afford to sacrifice the team’s defensive ceiling while he plays with those levers. The addition of Konsa was a personnel change that allowed Arsenal to remain the same.

Leeds transfer news: Will Lankshear January hopes shot down by 44-goal striker

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (483 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 25 Nov 2026 11:33.
  • Former Leeds United striker Brian Deane, speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, has played down the Whites' chances of signing Will Lankshear in the January transfer window.
  • The former Tottenham Hotspur youngster has taken the Championship by storm since moving to the Riverside Stadium in the summer, scoring 14 goals in 15 second-tier appearances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 25 Nov 2026 11:33.

Former Leeds United striker Brian Deane, speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, has played down the Whites' chances of signing Will Lankshear in the January transfer window.

The former Tottenham Hotspur youngster has taken the Championship by storm since moving to the Riverside Stadium in the summer, scoring 14 goals in 15 second-tier appearances.

Lankshear netted the winner as Middlesbrough beat Swansea City 2-1 on Tuesday night, a result that saw Kim Hellberg's men move one point clear of Wolverhampton Wanderers at the top of the Championship table.

The 21-year-old unsurprisingly sits top of the Championship top scorers charts, three clear of closest challenger Andri Gudjohnsen of Blackburn Rovers in the race for the Golden Boot.

Lankshear's form has inevitably led to speculation surrounding a swift return to the Premier League, with multiple clubs believed to be interested in securing his services, including Leeds.

Former club Tottenham, Arsenal, Brighton & Hove Albion and Newcastle United have also been credited with an interest, although Middlesbrough's £70m asking price could deter suitors.

Now, former Leeds forward Deane - who scored 44 goals in 199 matches for the Whites - has expressed his view that Lankshear should remain at the Riverside Stadium over the winter.

“This is his breakout season, and he is at a good club," Deane told Sports Mole. "Middlesbrough look on course to challenge for promotion, so hopefully he gets there with them.

According to recent reports, “He will be ambitious and attract attention from clubs such as Leeds, Brighton and Newcastle. He would be a good addition to a squad. But for his own development, I think he is in a good place at Middlesbrough.”.

Lankshear made just six senior appearances for Tottenham before being sold in a £9.8m deal over the summer, and the striker's contract with Middlesbrough does not expire until 2031.

A young striker scoring for fun in the Championship will always attract glances from top-tier clubs, but Lankshear may struggle to force his way into Daniel Farke's first XI right now.

First-choice pairing Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Noah Okafor boast a respectable nine Premier League goals between them in 2026-27, and as long as both are fit, they will spearhead Farke's 3-5-2 system.

Calvert-Lewin is now in the final 24 months of his contract at Elland Road, but the England international is understood to be close to signing a new Leeds deal.

Lukas Nmecha also provides a steady backup option, although he is due to become a free agent in 2027 and may seek a move away in January if his game-time situation does not improve.

However, Nmecha's proposed exit would then open the door for summer signing Jean-Matteo Bahoya to earn more opportunities, so a winter move for Lankshear would make little sense for all involved.

Brian Deane was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of BetWright.

#117735. Rare-variant genetic architecture of height in over 1.4 million individuals
