Andoni Iraola has now managed to get Liverpool to fourth in the Premier League table.

Obviously, this is still miles away from where they need to be but, the fact that only seven points separate them and first-placed Arsenal is excellent news.

Right now, it's unclear where Liverpool are going to finish in England's top flight but, if they keep performing to the standard they showed on Sunday against Manchester United, they'll be storming their way up the table.

But, for them to do this, improvements need to be made to their squad as, all of their other title rivals will be adding extra firepower to their ranks.

So, the fact that the January transfer window is now just over a month away is rather exciting.

Especially with all the players that they've just been linked with.

Liverpool see Gustavo Varela as a 'long-term target'.

Liverpool have several problem areas among their ranks that need addressing.

Obviously, since they're one of the biggest clubs in the world, they won't have any problem finding players who want to join.

However, the prices that Premier League clubs have to pay instantly have extra money added on top of them.

That's why only a certain number of deals can be struck by Liverpool in each window.

Moves for the future are also laid out with a new revision from Football Insider sharing that the Reds' recent links with Monza striker Gustavo Varela are for the 'long-term' rather than the short-term.

"Liverpool will not prioritise a move to sign Monza striker Gustavo Varela in January, sources have told Football Insider," they wrote.

"The 21-year-old has emerged as a target for the Reds, having struck 11 goals from his opening 11 games in Serie A so far this term.

"The Reds are "keeping tabs" on the Portuguese youngster, with several top Italian clubs also having their "eyes fixed on him" at the moment.

"However, sources say that Varela is viewed as more of a long-term option at Anfield, and the club are not likely to make a move for him this winter.

"Monza are relaxed over their frontman's future for now, but they know that further interest from top clubs is inevitable if he continues to perform.".

Liverpool's interest in Gustavo Varela could mean that they're changing to a two striker formation.

Liverpool only have two fit strikers among their ranks at the moment.

Alexander Isak is one of them and, since he was the Reds' record signing, he's obviously going to be Iraola's striker.

Lewis Koumas is the other and, even though his manager likes him, the fact that Hugo Ekitike is edging closer to a return will certainly worry him.

Before he got injured last term, Ekitike was easily Liverpool's best player and, they probably wouldn't have qualified for the Champions League if it wasn't for him.

So, the fact that Varela is now emerging as a potential option for the Reds on their shortlist certainly raises a few questions.

The easiest explanation for this move would be that, eventually, Iraola wants to move to a two striker formation while having Varela and Koumas as his back-up options.

Obviously, there are now guarantees that this will play out like that but, if that is the case, a major tactical change could be on its way to Anfield in the next couple of years.

#117688. Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival

📅 06 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1035 w)

Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1035 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In 2025, an international trial found that people treated for colon cancer were more likely to be alive eight years later if they had received long-term exercise coaching.
  • The question facing doctors now is less whether people with cancer should exercise, and rather how they should build it into routine care.
  • Yet experts caution that the trial's findings may not apply to every cancer or every patient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 2025, an international trial found that people treated for colon cancer were more likely to be alive eight years later if they had received long-term exercise coaching.

The question facing doctors now is less whether people with cancer should exercise, and rather how they should build it into routine care. In the US, that shift is reaching hospital standards. From January 2027, breast cancer centers must screen patients' physical function and recommend exercise or physical therapy where needed.

Yet experts caution that the trial's findings may not apply to every cancer or every patient.

The 2025 trial, called CHALLENGE, was led by the Canadian Cancer Trials Group. It began enrolling patients in 2009 and published its results in 2025.

The trial's 889 participants came from six countries, most from Canada and Australia. All had finished surgery and chemotherapy for stage 2 or 3 colon cancer, which had not spread to distant organs.

Half received only health education materials on exercise and healthy eating. The other half additionally met a physical activity consultant for three years.

According to recent reports, in the exercise group, the target was similar to adding 45 to 60 minutes of brisk walking, three to four times a week. The amount and type of activity varied from person to person, remarked Tormod Skogstad Nilsen, a cancer exercise researcher in Norway. But he said participants achieved lasting increases in their physical activity.

Exercise helped. People in the exercise group were less likely to see their cancer come back, to develop a new cancer or to die. In all, 93 had at least one of these setbacks, compared with 131 in the health education group.

According to recent reports, in cancer research, living longer usually means a larger share of people is still alive at a given point. It does not promise anyone a set number of extra years.

It has been revealed that eight years after joining CHALLENGE, about 90 of every 100 people in the exercise group were alive, compared with about 83 of every 100 in the health education group. That is about 7% more people alive in the group who had guided exercise.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

For people without cancer, the evidence comes from studies that follow people's habits and health over many years. These can show a link, but not prove cause and effect. Active people may also eat better or smoke less.

It has been revealed that in another 2025 study, more than 85,000 adults in the United Kingdom wore a wrist tracker for a week. Over about six years, those who moved most had a 26% lower risk of 13 cancers, including breast and colorectal cancer, than those who moved least.

According to recent reports, even light activity, such as household chores, was linked to lower risk. The link held after researchers accounted for lifestyle, weight and other health conditions.

Industry observers note that earlier research, based on people's self-reporting, has led to similar conclusions. A 2016 analysis of 1.44 million adults in the US and Europe linked free-time activity to a lower risk of many cancers, largely regardless of weight or smoking.

A trial to prove prevention is unlikely: Many cancers take years to develop, so it would need huge numbers of people followed for a long time.

According to recent reports, CHALLENGE included only people with colon cancer. But how it picked participants offers a clue: Before joining, they had to pass a fitness test.

Anna Campbell, a professor of clinical exercise science at Edinburgh Napier University in Scotland, sees that as a guide.

In a recent development, "I think patients with any other cancer stage II and III who have a reasonable baseline level of fitness and no major comorbidities that would prevent them from undertaking moderate to vigorous activity could be considered for similar interventions," she said. Comorbidities are other health conditions.

According to recent reports, nilsen noted some people decline to join exercise trials because they feel too unwell or tired, or do not want to exercise. "Hence, study populations are typically younger, 'healthier', and most times slightly more motivated compared to a clinical population," he mentioned.

The coaching aimed to make activity a lasting habit, and Campbell said that is where the trial's value lies.

"The main success of the study is that it enabled the participants to become independent exercisers staying active in a safe and effective and individualized way," she stated.

Nilsen agreed. Helping people become more active "in their own environment," without depending on a well-equipped training center, "would likely lead to more sustainable activity behavioral changes," he mentioned.

In a recent development, he is wary of fixed targets, however. "Exercise should be tailored to each individual and the challenges they face, rather than striving to reach a given minimum of exercise required," though health care resources may not always allow it, he added.

It has been revealed that in a 2024 survey of 549 people with cancer, only one in 10 had been referred to an exercise service. Yet almost three in four thought their oncologist should raise the subject.

"There are some excellent examples of effective pathways but these are few and far between," stated Campbell. Good services bring everyone on board, from surgeons to community fitness instructors.

"Ideally, one person in the clinical setting needs to champion the program to link all the team together.".

Industry observers note that campbell expects CHALLENGE's regular coaching will be cut back in everyday care. Apps and live online group sessions could still work, she said, if run by properly trained staff.

One recent study of live online exercise engaged patients from poorer backgrounds, in rural areas and with advanced cancer. "It answered some of the barriers, such as cost, travel and lack of confidence," she noted.

Patients can ask their care team what exercise is safe for them and what support exists.

Industry observers note that according to Nilsen, a training session can bring structure and company. "You made it here, despite your feeling unwell or fatigued this morning, so you feel mastery based on that," he noted.

  • In a recent development, arsenal can play world-class football and completely dominate teams for long spells, but lack the world-class attack to make the most of that domination, the sort of players you just know will create and convert major chances when the time comes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday raised some very familiar concerns and, if we’re being honest, revealed nothing we didn’t already know.

In a recent development, arsenal can play world-class football and completely dominate teams for long spells, but lack the world-class attack to make the most of that domination, the sort of players you just know will create and convert major chances when the time comes. And the way the team is starting games after the break is worrying, with teams who are battered to within an inch of their lives early on suddenly able to compete.

It has been revealed that I really feel like I could write two versions of today’s blog. One where I’m miserable, of course: the players can’t shoot, they make all the wrong choices in the decisive moment, we can’t keep wasting chances and dropping off after the break, if Andrea Berta doesn’t deliver the true heirs to Thierry Henry and Robert Pires in January, then he should be stuffed into one of the cannons outside the Armoury and fired into the cold night air.

The other version is much more glass half full: Arteta is coaching masterclasses every week, this level of dominance in games is something I could only dream of a few years ago, that’s the most shots we’ve had in a game all season, we’re top of the league, we’re creating loads without any set-piece reliance and without Bukayo Saka – the goals will come.

In a recent development, some people reading this would prefer (and relate better to) one version, and others the other version, I’m sure. Let’s see where we end up!

There were, as there tends to be in these Champions League games, a fair few changes from the weekend. Kepa, Piero Hincapie, Ben White, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Christos Tzolis, and Viktor Gyokeres all came into the team.

Despite featuring half a different side, there were plenty of parallels with the Newcastle match. Arsenal were dominant from the off, with Hincapie and White taking turns to play off of Gyokeres. Dortmund had no idea how to cover them and both fullbacks were the targets of early crosses into the box.

According to recent reports, after a couple of long-range efforts, Arsenal got their goal they deserved, with Gyokeres launching a ferocious, dipping effort beyond Gregor Kobel. The Swede can put his foot through the ball, that’s for sure, and the Dortmund backline gave him the sort of time and space to set himself that he doesn’t often get.

The pressure continued after the opener for a while, with Tzolis forcing a good save and Madueke just unable to sort his feet to tap in the rebound.

It’s fair to say the game settled down after 15/20 minutes, with Dortmund growing into it a little, but it was still Arsenal who looked like scoring the next goal. Rice shot over from almost the same patch of grass Gyokeres had scored from, and the midfielder had another chance when a beautiful one-touch move ended with him bursting through, hurtling towards the Dortmund box. Maybe he could’ve picked out Madueke in support, but he went alone and Nico Schlotterbeck just got across to block the shot.

Sources indicate that another huge chance was denied by the offside flag as much as the finishing – Madueke won the ball high, Odegaard squared it to Gyokeres, and the Swede fired over from near the penalty spot. Odegaard was ruled offside but I’m not convinced: had the ball hit the net, I think we’d have seen a very tight VAR check.

There was one thought on everyone’s minds at half-time: don’t do the same thing again. After Slavia Prague and Newcastle, do not do the same thing again.

Arsenal did the same thing again.

There was an early warning sign with Dortmund sliding the ball across the box and Maximilian Beier kicking the air. He didn’t make the same mistake with his next opportunity. Centre-back Joane Gadou (who was very impressive all evening) charged through the heart of the pitch before playing the ball to Beier, who jinked to unbalance Gabriel and slotted home.

Industry observers note that sometimes a goal is just a good goal, and I don’t think anyone was really at fault here. It’s a great run from Gadou, Beier tricks Gabriel to take the ball onto his weaker left side – it’s fair if Gabriel is expecting (and blocking the angle) on the attacker’s favoured foot, I know how that can happen. I think if we score that goal we’re talking about two brilliant individuals, rather than defensive errors.

Industry observers note that my first thought? Not again. My second? OK, how do we respond? Because on Saturday, the response was poor.

Sources indicate that this time it was a lot better. Jobe Bellingham had a rebound disallowed for offside, a moment that really brought the crowd back into the game, but in truth, that was Dortmund’s only real moment of threat. From the goal on 55 minutes to full-time, Arsenal had 15 shots to Dortmund’s two.

And that doesn’t include Serhou Guirassy playing one-twos with the post after a clever, low free-kick from Martin Odegaard late on.

Recent findings suggest that madueke had an effort blocked. Gyokeres flicked a header wide. Madueke shot wide beyond the far post after a good run. Gyokeres missed a substantial chance with his head from six yards out. Rice hit the near post from a tight angle after a brilliant pass from Eberechi Eze.

A couple of late corners came to nothing, and that was it.

Mikel Arteta was clearly pleased with the performance on the whole:.

Recent findings suggest that well, I think I love the way the team played. There’s no question how superior, how dominant, how much of a threat we were, how connected everybody was to the game … It was great to watch. It was unbelievable that sometimes the ball hasn’t ended up in the back of the net. That’s my feeling.

to do what we’ve done out there is just something to be very, very pleased about, because there is very little more that we can demand from the team.

But we all know what that little more is:.

obviously the feeling is that we should reward ourselves much more when you put that kind of performance, the amount of chances, the situation, and even shots that are not there. We are three against two, two against one, and the ball doesn’t land with the right person. There is an element of luck, there is an element of us finishing the actions better. We need to insist, because I think what the team has done and shown today is the right direction.

Often when Arsenal don’t win games, it feels like it’s because the team haven’t created enough chances. We end up focusing on that one moment, where that one player didn’t execute the way you wanted. But last night wasn’t one of those: Arsenal didn’t struggle to turn dominance into good, slick football, and that football into a healthy number of decent opportunities.

That’s incredibly frustrating, but I do think you win a lot more often than not when you do that. Maybe that’s a hard sell for some this morning, but it’s how I feel about it when we play well, especially when we’ve been winning games anyway. That’s the first time this season we’ve gone two without a win across all competitions, and we’ve won 14 of 19 games so far. Sometimes things don’t fall for you, and this one felt a lot like ‘one of those’, certainly more than Newcastle did.

A word for a couple of promising performances too, with the boss asked about Gyokeres in his post-match press conference:.

What I love the most is how connected he was to the team. We used him many times in different ways. His link-up play, the way he held the ball, the way he threw it in behind and stretched the pitch. There was a lot to like in that performance and that’s the victory that we need.

His finishing was off after the brilliant opener, but at least he was in the positions: too often this season and last, Gyokeres has gone through a game barely registering a shot. He had seven last night, and if he can do that more often he’ll score a lot more. His general play was improved too, both holding the ball up and competing in behind.

And I thought Martin Odegaard was excellent too. His eight chances created from open play was the most of any player in any Champions League match so far this season.

It has been revealed that since we returned to the competition in 2023, we’ve had a player create more than five chances in a match just twice: Odegaard at Napoli in September (6) and Odegaard last night (9). He’s incredibly unlucky not to be leaving the game with a couple of assists.

The draw leaves us in a decent position to finish in the all-crucial top eight in the league phase still, although you have to squint a bit to see us landing in the also-important top two. Real Madrid are up next and that’s a reminder of the sort of teams we’re up against: finishing in the top two is a tall order at the best of times.

With each passing game, it is impossible not to wonder what could be done in January to add to the team. Unless there’s a sudden uptick out of nowhere, those thoughts aren’t disappearing. And even if there is a massive uptick, those thoughts will still be around. But 30 shots is the most we’ve had in a game all season, and the same group of players have scored more goals with fewer shots (/chances) plenty of times. Let’s hope we see some more clinical finishing on Sunday.

Guess I landed on the glass half full version.

According to recent reports, there should be an Arsecast once Blogs has caught up with the game, so stay tuned for that. Enjoy your Wednesdays!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool have a lot of decisions to make before the end of the 2026-27 season.

Right now, they don't really look like they're going to be able to compete for the Premier League title or the Champions League.

Indeed, there are only seven points between them and first-placed Arsenal but, considering the Reds have already been beaten by Mikel Arteta's men once this season, that gap is going to be hard to break down.

Obviously, if they end up drawing or losing a couple of games like they did against Newcastle on Saturday, they could be in with a chance but, if it ends up being down to Liverpool, fans wouldn't really hold out much hope.

That is, especially since they were beaten 3-2 in the Champions League by Fenerbahce.

Changes are clearly needed at Anfield which is why the upcoming transfer windows are going to be massive for them.

Liverpool would have to slash Ronald Araujo's buy clause in half to sign him permanently.

Nobody knows what Liverpool are going to do in the winter or summer transfer windows.

They have thrown their hat into many different rings with almost every position among their ranks covered by a fresh target or two.

Some players that the Reds have been linked with have been exciting for fans but others, not so much.

There are also some decisions to make about their current crop of players with Ronald Araujo's future being one of the most talked-about deals in the world.

Within their season-long loan deal, Liverpool have a €55 million option to buy the Uruguayan and, even though he's performed rather well, the Reds are still undecided about whether they want to activate that option to buy or not.

And, now, thanks to an update from David Lynch via Anfield Index, it's now clear what Liverpool's aims are.

"That figure [€55 million] is far too high for Liverpool to be interested," he mentioned.

"You’re talking it would have to be, I reckon, about even half that much to even give a sniff of Liverpool being interested.".

Liverpool need to make their decision on Ronald Araujo soon.

Although there is still a long while until June comes around, a decision on Araujo needs to be made.

He's at the moment Liverpool's first-choice right-back and, without him among their ranks, even more problems would be coming the Reds' way.

Obviously, his prior experience of La Liga and the Champions League has massively helped him adjust to Premier League life but, since he's 27 years old and has a rather ropey injury history, it feels like a lot of money for Liverpool to commit to.

That is, especially when they don't know how good Conor Bradley is going to be upon his return from injury.

Everything is up in the air at then moment but, even if they don't want to, a decision is going to have to be made soon.

Otherwise, the Reds could end up missing out on the "physically dominant" defender or going for someone who's worse than the Uruguayan which would be far from ideal.

Tomorrow evening, AC Milan will entrust Ardon Jashari with the job of filling Luka Modric’s shoes, after the Croatian’s injury.

If you missed last night’s reporting, Milan have been dealt a bit of a blow ahead of their game against Olympiacos, as Modric has suffered a muscle strain. It’s not a major one, and he should be back for next weekend’s game.

Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, it creates a short-term issue and in a midfield where only a few names have convinced, it plunges Ruben Amorim into the water somewhat. There is a solution, though, and it would be ideal if he stepped up.

In a recent development, since he arrived, Jashari has been seen as the next in line for Modric, but he’s never shown performances to match that eventual rise. However, Gazzetta dello Sport (as seen below) write that he could take that step against Olympiacos.

In a recent development, it’s a potential turning point for the Swiss, who still has the faith of the club and the fans, especially after his first goal at the weekend. So, with it being a necessity that he comes into the team here, a solid performance is needed.

It has been revealed that it opens a space for Jashari, but filling Modric’s boots will not be an easy task. In fact, he’ll have to be at his best to replace him, especially in a game with so much on the line.

Sources indicate that looking at the Europa League table, the Rossoneri need to be perfect if they’re to have any chance of a top eight finish. For him, though, Jashari must be perfect if his journey at San Siro is to continue.

So far, his time in Italy has been marred by injury and a failure to establish himself as a starter, or even a key rotational option. Yet, the Diavolo never gave up on him, refusing a sale in the summer.

In a recent development, now, it is time to repay that in a game where ‘everything looks different’. For Jashari, it’s a simple task: be solid. He’s got a guaranteed place, reliable teammates around him and the trust to act.

In a recent development, no one can challenge him for the next five days; the spot is guaranteed. It’ll be up to him if those five days become 10 or more. If not, there’s a market waiting for him.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 25 Nov 2026 14:16, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 14:19.

On Friday, the Columbus Crew can pull off what may become the biggest upset in MLS playoff history and eliminate Inter Miami in game two of that first-round series at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field.

Last weekend the Crew took game one by a 3-0 score, putting them in position to eliminate the reigning champions should they win this upcoming fixture.

Columbus had a lot of momentum heading into the playoffs, and that continued on Saturday as they took advantage of some sloppy Miami defending to take a surprising lead in this series.

Laurent Courtois has seen his side score three or more goals in four of their last five matches versus MLS opposition, while posting a clean sheet in three of those instances, making them an appealing option to choose on the UK betting sites.

The Crew exposed gaps in the Miami squad, scoring on three of their five targeted efforts last weekend and putting the Herons on the ropes heading into game two.

This is only the second time they are up 1-0 since this best-of-three first-round format was introduced, with this team advancing past Atlanta United in three games on the only previous occasion in which they were in this position in 2023.

Only once since their 2015 MLS Cup final defeat versus the Portland Timbers have they lost a post-season match at home, with the Upcoming York Red Bulls blanking them 1-0 in game one of that opening round series in 2024.

Friday will mark the second time the Crew can eliminate Miami from a major competition in Columbus, after knocking them out of the 2024 Leagues Cup thanks to a 3-2 victory at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field in the round of 16.

For a team boasting so much experience and talent in the biggest club and international competitions, Inter Miami failed to keep their composure in numerous instances last weekend.

Saturday’s defeat was the joint-worst for the club in the post-season, though given everything that transpired, they could be looking much worse heading into this match.

Kily Gonzalez will be relieved to know that Lionel Messi is available, escaping with just a caution in game one after throwing the ball at Gonzalo Tapia, a moment some believed should have warranted a sending off for the Argentine.

Miami played a good portion of that match a man down, and have never won the second game in a best-of-three MLS playoff series.

The Herons have given up a combined six goals in their last two matches versus MLS opposition and have yet to beat an MLS club in a knockout fixture this season.

The reigning league champions have lost four of their five all-time playoff outings away from home, with their only triumph coming at FC Cincinnati in 2025 (4-0).

Columbus Crew Major League Soccer form:.

Columbus Crew form (all competitions):.

Inter Miami Major League Soccer form:.

Due to a cruciate ligament tear, Wessam Abou Ali will not be available for Columbus in game two of this series.

Gonzalo Tapia netted twice in Miami, with Taha Habroune also scoring as Patrick Schulte made three stops for the clean sheet.

On the Miami side, Mateo Silvetti is dealing with a shoulder matter, Tadeo Allende still has a knee problem and Israel Boatwright is recovering from a cruciate ligament tear.

Gonzalo Lujan will be suspended following his red card in game one, while Sergio Reguilon, David Ayala and Cesar Abadia are all questionable with lower-body injuries.

Columbus Crew possible starting lineup:.

Schulte; Farsi, Moreira, Zawadzki, Amundsen; Zaroury, Chambost, Habroune, Rodriguez, Tapia, Mendez.

Inter Miami possible starting lineup:.

St. Clair; Fray, Casemiro, Micael, Falcon; De Paul, Bright, Segovia; Messi, Suarez, Berterame.

While Miami have all they need to come back and win this series, they are far too rigid defensively and give away too many quality scoring opportunities, which is why we believe their season will end much earlier than most would have expected.

De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4118 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2. However, the development of such peptides at both targets is challenging, limited primarily by low design success rates and weak bioactivity. Here we present ORIDTP, an artificial intelligence platform that integrates single-target knowledge transfer and dual-target reinforcement to enable the rational design of high-potency peptides. ORIDTP successfully designed dual-target co-agonists for the GLP-1R and glucagon receptor (GCGR, also known as GLR), six of which surpassed the strongest natural binders of each receptor in bioactivity. Notably, the lead peptide GA-Dual.R5.S3 induced substantial weight loss and glycaemic improvement in diet-induced obese mice, and exhibited pronounced antidiabetic effects in db/db mice, without inducing nausea or aversion. Furthermore, ORIDTP demonstrated generalizability through successful zero-shot design of dual-target co-inhibitors for structurally and mechanistically distinct immune checkpoints, PD-1 and CTLA-4. Out of 15 designed peptides, 8 blocked both checkpoint interactions and 3 further exhibited in vivo antitumour efficacy in human checkpoint knock-in tumour-bearing mice. The lead peptide IC-Dual.P3 achieved the strongest tumour growth suppression, reducing tumour volume by 94.2% relative to controls. Together, these findings establish ORIDTP as a powerful and generalizable platform for de novo dual-target peptide discovery.

Report: Andoni Iraola wants to bring versatile defensive sensation to Liverpool soon

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (550 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Andoni Iraola's time as Liverpool's manager has delivered a bit of a mixed bag of performances so far.
  • The Spaniard was brought in to replace Arne Slot after the Dutchman led his title-defending team to a fifth-place finish.
  • Clearly, this performance was nowhere near good enough for a title-defending team and, change was definitely needed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola's time as Liverpool's manager has delivered a bit of a mixed bag of performances so far.

The Spaniard was brought in to replace Arne Slot after the Dutchman led his title-defending team to a fifth-place finish.

Clearly, this performance was nowhere near good enough for a title-defending team and, change was definitely needed.

And, even though over £150 million worth of change came through the Anfield doors in the summer, more deals need to be struck so that Liverpool can start competing for silverware again.

So, even though the transfer window isn't open yet, there's no reason for the rumour mill to not continue turning.

Liverpool are eyeing a move for Mohamed Simakan.

Alongside Liverpool's attack, their defence has been a major problem for them.

Whether its been a lack of form or just the sheer number of injuries they've suffered, things just haven't gone to plan for Liverpool's back line over the last couple of years.

That's why players such as Jeremy Jacquet, Ronald Araujo and Giovanni Leoni have all been brought in.

Right now, things are in a good place for the Reds' back four but, that could all change if they choose against signing Araujo permanently.

Nothing is set in stone yet but, the fact that Caught Offside have shared that Mohamed Simakan is now wanted by Liverpool proves that Iraola and Julian Ward are trying to line up some back-up options just in case things don't go to blueprint.

"Liverpool and Manchester United are both monitoring Mohamed Simakan as the Premier League rivals consider defensive reinforcements ahead of 2027," they wrote.

"The 26-year-old has remained an important figure for Al-Nassr since leaving RB Leipzig and offers the kind of profile that could appeal to both clubs.

"Comfortable at centre-back or right-back, Simakan combines pace and physical strength with experience playing in an aggressive defensive system.

For Liverpool and United, however, January may be too early for anything concrete. For Liverpool, Simakan’s versatility is particularly attractive.

"With long-term succession planning required in central defence, signing a player capable of operating centrally while also covering right-back would give the squad valuable flexibility.".

Mohamed Simakan could become Liverpool's next Ronald Araujo.

One of the best things about Araujo is that he can comfortably play as a right-back or a centre-back.

No matter which position he's used in, he's always been seen as one of the Reds' best players this term with fans demanding that his deal is made permanent.

Clearly, this hasn't happened yet and, since rumours have been emerging that the price of Araujo would have to be slashed in half for Liverpool to even consider doing that, the deal doesn't feel all that likely to come to fruition.

This isn't ideal news but, the fact that Simakan can be used as a centre-back or a right-back does mean that change is coming to Anfield.

He may have spent the last couple of years in the Saudi Pro League with Al-Nassr but, he's still only 26 years old so, even if he isn't up to scratch right away, he could develop and become better.

Nothing is set in stone yet but, since Iraola wants to bring him in, Simakan could end up being a name that Liverpool's fans get rather used to.

Five Man United players who could leave in January as part of major Mauricio Pochettino clear-out

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (720 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Matt Law | 25 Nov 2026 14:30, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 14:32.
  • Manchester United are expected to be active during the January transfer window, with the club potentially making three mid-season signings.
  • The Red Devils presently find themselves down in 19th spot in the Premier League table and facing what would be a stunning relegation from the top flight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 25 Nov 2026 14:30, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 14:32.

Manchester United are expected to be active during the January transfer window, with the club potentially making three mid-season signings.

The Red Devils presently find themselves down in 19th spot in the Premier League table and facing what would be a stunning relegation from the top flight.

There could also be first-team departures in the winter market, as newly introduced head coach Mauricio Pochettino begins to shape the squad.

Here, Sports Mole looks at five players who could potentially leave Old Trafford when the January market opens for business.

Zirkzee was linked with a move away from Man United over the summer, but he was ultimately not allowed to depart due to the fact that the Red Devils were unable to sign a replacement.

Even with Benjamin Sesko out injured, Zirkzee has not started a single match this season, with each of his 11 appearances coming off the bench.

The Netherlands international has scored twice this season, but his overall record for Man United since arriving from Bologna in 2024 is 11 goals in 86 appearances.

It has been a struggle for the 25-year-old in English football, but he is not short of interest, and a return to Serie A in January is seen as a serious possibility at this stage.

Como and Napoli are the latest clubs to be linked with Zirkzee.

Mazraoui is reportedly attracting the attention of AC Milan ahead of the January market, with a mid-season departure for the Morocco international thought to be possible.

The 29-year-old has underperformed in his nine appearances for Man United this season and is not believed to be in the club's long-term aims.

Initially, the defender impressed after arriving from Bayern Munich, and he has now represented the Red Devils on 86 occasions in all competitions.

However, a switch in the January market could be on the cards, especially if Man United are able to boost their options at full-back in the winter window.

Heaven is reportedly open to the idea of leaving Man United during the winter market.

The 20-year-old has made eight appearances for the Red Devils this season, including five outings in the Premier League, but he was an unused substitute against Liverpool in the team's last match, which ended in a 4-0 defeat.

Man United are expected to bring in a new centre-back in January, and Heaven is noted to be concerned over what that would mean for his playing time.

As a result, the Englishman is allegedly open to a winter loan move, while a permanent exit is not being ruled out depending on what offers arrive.

Real Salt Lake will try to extend their season into next week with a Friday win over the Vancouver Whitecaps at America First Field in game two of that best-of-three playoff series.

The reigning MLS Cup runners-up captured game one 2-0 last Sunday, putting them one win away from round two in the Western Conference playoffs.

After surviving a nervy shootout in the Wild Card Round, Salt Lake are now on the brink of elimination yet again after a subpar showing in game one against the Caps.

On Sunday, Pablo Mastroeni’s men suffered just their second defeat in their last eight MLS outings and were second-best for much of the game.

While they are on the verge of another early exit, they can draw optimism from being unbeaten in their last four MLS affairs at America First Field.

During the regular season, Salt Lake indicated strong attacking potency on home soil, netting three or more goals six times and scoring multiple times on 12 separate occasions.

They will try to end a five-match playoff losing run on Friday, scoring a goal or fewer in each of those instances.

Claret and Cobalt have not lost a playoff match at home in 90 minutes this decade, with their only such victory at America First Field occurring on penalties versus the Houston Dynamo in game two of that opening round series.

It is just one game, but Vancouver looked very much like title contenders as they began the 2026 MLS post-season in style.

Jesper Sorensen’s side carried the play throughout game one and will seek a fifth consecutive MLS triumph on Friday.

While this is the fourth straight year the Caps are in the post-season, they have won only once in that span in normal time away from home, beating San Diego 3-1 in the Western Conference Final last year.

Meanwhile, they failed to win three of their final four regular-season away fixtures this season against Western Conference opposition, with the highest-scoring team in the West failing to score on two of those occasions.

Vancouver have never lost a playoff encounter under Sorensen when netting first but have also never won a post-season outing in 90 minutes when conceding the opener under his leadership.

Sorensen, meanwhile, has won every match against RSL as the Caps boss, including their last two visits to America First Field, in which his team scored three goals both times.

Vancouver Whitecaps Major League Soccer form:.

Due to a hamstring strain, Ariath Piol may miss this match for RSL, while Diego Luna and Emeka Eneli are questionable because of knee injuries and Zach Booth still has to clear concussion protocol.

Sergi Solans has scored three goals in his last two MLS home outings, including the opener in their 2-1 win over the Los Angeles Galaxy on Decision Day, while Rafael Cabral kept game one close, making six saves, many of them spectacular.

On the Vancouver side, an illness may keep Belal Halbouni out on Friday, and it is unlikely we will see Kenji Cabrera feature as he deals with a foot injury.

Edier Ocampo got the Caps on the board late in the opening half of game one, with Bruno Caicedo adding some insurance in the final 45 minutes.

What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (598 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that since its inception in 1990, the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship has almost always been held in the spring — apart from 2021 and 2022, when the COVID-19 pandemic saw it moved to the summer.
  • Recent findings suggest that the idea is make it easier for all of the world's best players to participate.
  • "This gives the women's game a unique selling point," International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) President Franz Reindl recently told the SID news agency.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that since its inception in 1990, the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship has almost always been held in the spring — apart from 2021 and 2022, when the COVID-19 pandemic saw it moved to the summer. This year, though, the tournament, being hosted by Denmark from November 6 to November 16, is being held in November for the first time.

Recent findings suggest that the idea is make it easier for all of the world's best players to participate. Since its inception in 2023, the North America-based Professional Women's Hockey League (PWHL), widely considered the world's best, has had to pause its season to allow players to take part in the Worlds. This is no longer necessary, as the PWHL's regular season doesn't open until December.

"This gives the women's game a unique selling point," International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) President Franz Reindl recently told the SID news agency. "Because the PWHL season begins after this, we can be certain that the very best players are participating.".

Recent findings suggest that previously, the teams were divided into a stronger group and a weaker group, with the idea being to avoid, as much as possible, lopsided scores. This is because women's hockey is not as balanced as the men's game, with Canada or the United States having won every tournament since its inception.

In a recent development, under the old system, all five teams in the stronger Group A advanced to the quarterfinals. Under the newly introduced format, four of the five teams advance from both groups. This also sees powerhouses the US and Canada in separate groups, meaning the marquee matchup can't occur early in the tournament.

Group A: USA, Czechia, Switzerland, Germany, Austria.

Group B: Canada, Finland, Sweden, Japan, Denmark.

Recent findings suggest that no. While the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled on October 30 — a week before the opening faceoff of the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship — that the IIHF must allow Russia back into its tournaments during the 2026-2027 season, it made no mention of this tournament. Under the CAS ruling though, the IIHF will be required to include Russia at the 2027 tournament in Quebec City.

As noted above, either Canada or the United States has won every edition of this tournament — and indeed the two countries have split Olympic gold medals between them (Canada with five, USA with three) since the sport was introduced to the Winter Games in 1998. There is nothing to suggest that this is about to change in Herning and Esbjerg, although Canada enters the tournament with a vastly different roster from the one that won Olympic silver in Milano in February.

Among those looking to break this North American domination are Finland, the only other team ever to have made it to a world championship final and Switzerland, who took bronze in Milan.

The United States and Canada will play in generic kits provided by the International Ice Hockey Federation's official supplier due to an ongoing commercial rights dispute.

It has been revealed that the Canadian federation, Hockey Canada, mentioned in a statement on Wednesday that its players would be wearing jerseys designed by True Hockey instead of their Bauer jerseys featuring the national team logo. USA Hockey has confirmed that its players too will be wearing jerseys without its national emblem.

"While we have yet to see the jersey Canada will be playing in on Friday, our team remains focused on the tournament and representing our country proudly on and off the ice," Hockey Canada said.

Report: Liverpool agreement with 'game-changer' edging closer

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (480 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Liverpool are currently fourth in the Premier League table.
  • If they finish in this position by the end of the term, they'll qualify for the Champions League again.
  • But, in reality, they should be aiming for a much higher finish.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool are currently fourth in the Premier League table.

If they finish in this position by the end of the term, they'll qualify for the Champions League again.

But, in reality, they should be aiming for a much higher finish.

They have spent over £600 million on fresh players across these last couple of years and, with that amount of spending, you'd expect them to be one of the best teams in the world.

That clearly isn't the case as, around a month ago now, they were beaten 3-2 by Fenerbahce which is probably their low point of the season.

However, this latest news to emerge from Anfield could change everything.

Liverpool and Rio Ngumoha are getting closer to agreeing a new deal.

One of the biggest stories to emerge from the 2026-27 season so far is about what's going to happen to Rio Ngumoha.

The Englishman was promoted to Liverpool's first-team squad by Arne Slot last term and, since then, he's never really looked back.

Talk of him extending his contract, which expires in 2028, has been rife since the 2026-27 season got fully underway with some rumours about him potentially switching Liverpool for Munich at some point.

Fortunately, this deal never came to fruition and now, the Reds are in the driving seat to lock him down.

And, thanks to a fresh update from TEAMtalk, that looks like exactly what's about to happen.

"Ngumoha is primed to put pen to paper on a new and much improved contract at Anfield," they wrote.

"Bayern Munich are once again sniffing around the player amid a raft of injuries and problems with their forward line.

"However, sources tell us Liverpool are close to finalising a new deal that will ensure Ngumoha continues to terrorise Premier League defences for years to come.".

Rio Ngumoha is the future of Liverpool's attack.

This season, Ngumoha has featured 15 times for Liverpool and has contributed to four goals.

Three of them have come as assists for his teammates and, whether he's been used on the left or right-wing, he's always put in plenty of effort.

As mentioned, Ngumoha's effort hasn't gone unnoticed with clubs such as Bayern Munich trying their hardest to strike a deal with him.

Obviously, Liverpool would never let that happen but it does prove how high the Englishman's ceiling actually is.

Right now, Ngumoha might not be a guaranteed starter but, in the future when certain players exit or Liverpool's tactics change, he's likely to be one of the first names on Liverpool's team sheet.

The former Chelsea man may only be 18 years old but, as long as Liverpool keep him around, their attack will be sorted for at least one attacker so, here's hoping these rumours of a deal being close to completion are true and that the Reds can lock their 'game-changer' down soon.

Two months ago there were many doom merchants insisting that Aston Villa were heading for a season of struggle, but they are looking foolish now.

After a summer of uncertainty and much change, Villa are stepping into a brave new era and find themselves joint-top of the Champions League table after three matches.

With co-owner Nassef Sawiris in attendance, Villa fans are dreaming of another magical season almost four years after Emery walked through the doors at this historic club.

Sawiris was the key figure driving Emery’s appointment in October 2022 and few could have predicted the success that has followed with the Basque manager at the helm.

Villa 2.0 have made a flawless start to their European campaign and are running into form in the Premier League after a sticky start.

Sources indicate that in this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are currently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

He said: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”.

Recent findings suggest that what a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

In a recent development, with six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 08:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:15 EST, 24 November 2026.

There are few transfers that get West Ham supporters talking quite like the sale of an academy graduate.

Who can forget the uproar after Grady Diangana joined West Brom in 2020, when club captain Mark Noble released a public statement voicing his anger and disappointment at the move.

Noble’s thoughts were echoed by team-mates at the time, while supporters were similarly up in arms at the sale of the winger.

So, when Freddie Potts joined Club Brugge for £10million on the eve of the season to mark the controversial departure of another product of the proclaimed Academy of Football, you can imagine the reaction.

Potts represented more than a graduate. A boyhood West Ham fan whose dad Steve is a club legend and still serves as a first-team coach, he joined the academy aged six. His brother Dan also came through the ranks.

The midfielder had just enjoyed a breakthrough campaign despite West Ham’s relegation, and many felt he was the perfect player to build their Championship promotion push around.

Freddie Potts is shining in Belgium with Club Brugge after joining from West Ham in the summer.

Potts joined the Hammers academy aged six and enjoyed a breakthrough year last season.

Hammers favourites Kevin Nolan and Tony Cottee weighed in with their disapproval at his sale, while celebrity fan Ray Winstone expressed his shock and anger live on talkSPORT.

In a recent development, ‘Of course you see it (the division about the move) on social media,’ Potts tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘Every player does. But even though last season was tough I always felt I had a connection with the West Ham fans.

It has been revealed that ‘No matter if I played well or bad I always felt I understood what it meant to play for West Ham. It's a great club with great fans and people. In the end, I had to do what was best for me. I wanted to play this season, and I felt like this was the best place to do that.’.

Potts, 22 at the time of his exit, admits it was extremely tough and emotional for him and his family to leave a club he had been at for 16 years.

But, during pre-season he became aware he wasn’t likely to play as much as he wanted to under Nuno Espirito Santo.

‘In the end it’s the manager’s decision,’ Potts states. ‘I wasn’t getting the minutes I wanted. The feeling was that I wasn’t guaranteed to be in the intends as much as Club Brugge were promising me, so I thought it was best for me to move.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It was very hard. West Ham have been my club my whole life and I have a lot of love for West Ham. But I had to take into account what was best for my career and I’m loving it at Brugge. It’s a really exciting place full of great people and a great manager.’.

Potts had multiple options in the summer, including Premier League interest, yet the chance to play in the Champions League and compete for titles with Brugge attracted him.

Their record of developing young players and a talented squad that includes the likes of Carlos Forbs and Nicolo Tresoldi was equally compelling, and the midfielder hasn't looked back.

Industry observers note that potts started Brugge’s first 10 league games, missing their final one before the international break due to suspension. He returned at the weekend as they thrashed Mechelen 5-1. Ivan Leko’s side are one point adrift of Union Saint-Gilloise at the top of the Belgian Pro League, and they have also impressed in the Champions League.

According to recent reports, in Europe, Brugge have beaten Inter Milan, PSV and Lens on their way to nine points from 12, only narrowly losing 3-2 to Aston Villa. Potts has started each match, including their memorable 4-3 win against Inter at the San Siro, and they host Liverpool on Wednesday.

It has been revealed that ‘It's a really good group of lads,’ he claims. ‘Everyone speaks English as well which helps me. It's a good team and we're happy playing with each other.’.

Industry observers note that he is clearly enjoying life and is just the fifth English player in history to play for the club. Potts did take time to settle though, and admits he initially suffered from homesickness.

‘I found it difficult because East London and Essex have been my home for my whole life,’ he claims. ‘West Ham was my life. It was tough in terms of moving into a upcoming language and everything but you get used to it and I’m really enjoying it here. It’ll be strange going back home to England.'.

Potts has been a regular and has had a key role in Brugge's impressive early exploits in Europe.

Brugge have beaten PSV, Lens and Inter Milan, and they take on Liverpool this Wednesday.

In a recent development, potts’ family have popped over to see him and he has enjoyed exploring his new surroundings. He is yet to learn the local language and scolds himself for being lazy for relying on English, although he has picked up little bits of Flemish.

He has immersed himself in the culture too, and reveals he has tried the world-famous Belgian fries and a few local beers, albeit only when he has enough time to recover between games.

Despite his new life in Europe, Potts remains a West Ham fan and tries to watch them on TV every week.

He has been surprised by their struggles on their return to the Championship for the first time in 14 years, with Nuno paying the price by losing his job. Former Hammers midfielder Scott Parker has since taken the reins.

According to recent reports, ‘I still think they're playing well,’ Potts says. ‘They've got a great team and Scott Parker is a really good manager. You get ups and downs but I still 100 per cent think West Ham will get promoted this year.'.

Recent findings suggest that potts’ stay in the Hammers first team may have been brief, yet there were still plenty of highs, not least a storming performance on his first Premier League start. That came in a win over Newcastle last November in the Hammers’ first home victory of the season. He was also coached by his dad, an experience he jokes had positives and negatives.

He left West Ham after realising he was unlikely to be first choice under Nuno Espirito Santo.

Potts is a boyhood West Ham fan and is fully expecting them to get promoted this season.

Attention now turns to Brugge’s clash against Liverpool. It promises to be a tricky challenge for Andoni Iraola’s side against a team who are determined to prove themselves on the European stage.

The two teams are level on points in the league phase, and Potts is keen for his side to take another scalp.

‘I don't think there's much difference in the way we've been performing in the Champions League,’ Potts concludes. ‘It'll be difficult for them to come to our place as well.

‘They're a great team, but we're going to approach it like we have with every Champions League game. We've gone away and beaten Milan, we've beaten PSV away. These are top teams.

‘Results like that give you a boost of how far you can go. You don't want to look too far ahead but every game in this competition is a chance to show everyone what you can do.

‘Liverpool will be a tough game but we've proved it against top teams before and we're going in thinking that we can do it again.’.

Latest Update: Preparing for 45C: How Germany tests its crisis response

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (757 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.
  • About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.
  • In a recent development, it is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.

About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.

In a recent development, it is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK). And it's been up and running for more than two decades.

Industry observers note that the first LÜKEX in 2004 dealt with the scenario of an extreme winter with a major power outage. Lessons from that exercise proved valuable in 2005 when the Münsterland region of North Rhine-Westphalia — Germany's most populous state — experienced the worst power outage in the country's postwar history. When heavy snowfall caused power lines to collapse, leaving 250,000 people without electricity for days, there was a better understanding of who to contact and where the bottlenecks were.

According to recent reports, since it first started, LÜKEX has trained for scenarios involving terror attacks, an influenza pandemic, biological health threats, storm floods in northern Germany and gas shortages in southern Germany. The most recent exercise in 2023 simulated a cyberattack targeting government operations.

With the help of other ministries, the German Weather Service and the Federal Institute of Hydrology, the BBK developed a drought risk analysis to serve as the scenario.

Participants, which include aid organizations Malteser and the German Red Cross, didn't know the specifics of the challenges they would be facing until the exercise kicked off on Wednesday.

It has been revealed that at that point, they were told it was July 20, 2027. In that simulated future, they find themselves in a Germany that has been struggling with extreme heat for weeks; water levels in rivers are falling, food supplies are becoming scarce and emergency services are under growing pressure.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Patrick Pöhler, spokesperson for Malteser, said additional details include supermarkets having run out of water, collapsed supply chains and skyrocketing prices to enter a swimming pool. He said the scenario also goes into how the situation is impacting sections of society.

Recent findings suggest that "Emergency services and elderly care are areas that require particular attention," Pöhler noted. "The increasingly extreme summers of recent years have shown how severely heat can affect staffing levels and operational capacity.".

In its scenario, the northern port city of Hamburg is tasked with managing the disruption of key transport routes that are impacting access to food and drinking water, as well as handling disinformation attacks that are fueling public fear.

"We have not conducted an exercise of this magnitude since the end of the Cold War. Yet such preparations are essential to strengthen our resilience and crisis-response capabilities," remarked Hamburg's minister for the interior, Andy Grote.

According to recent reports, LÜKEX is designed to test and strengthen the country's ability to manage major crises at a strategic level. No matter the specific scenario, they all help test internal structures, workflows and decision-making processes.

"The lessons learned are continuously incorporated into improving preparedness, planning and cooperation in civil protection," noted BBK spokesperson Katharina Böcker.

Sources indicate that this year's topic was decided a long time ago, well before recent summers in which Germany experienced extreme heat, she added. Thousands of people died from heat-related causes during the hot months of this year.

"Crises such as extreme heat waves and prolonged droughts can affect large parts of the population and challenge the operational capabilities of our critical structures over an extended period," noted Christian Reuter, secretary general of the German Red Cross, another organization taking part.

Observers take note of how organizations react in the crisis scenario to find out what went well and where things didn't run smoothly.

"We are explicitly encouraged to make mistakes," stated Malteser's Pöhler, because that is how weaknesses can be identified and addressed.

A first internal debrief is scheduled for Friday, he added.

Sources indicate that A preliminary report with the main findings and respective recommendations is due to be published in the first quarter of next year. A full evaluation report will then be released later in the third quarter of 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 25 Nov 2026 16:48.

Maritimo and Nacional renew their Madeira derby rivalry in the Primeira Liga on Friday evening, with both sides looking to claim an notable victory and move further clear of the drop zone.

The two clubs are meeting in the top flight for the first time in five years, with the visitors sitting 13th in the Primeira Liga table on 10 points from 11 matches, just two points above the 15th-placed hosts, who have a game in hand against Estoril Praia and sit outside the relegation playoff place on head-to-head points ahead of Casa Pia.

Maritimo made an encouraging start to life back in the top flight, winning their opening two league fixtures against Casa Pia and Famalicao, but they have not claimed another Primeira Liga victory since beating the latter on August 16.

Mitchell van der Gaag's side have since gone eight league matches without a win (D2, L6), including defeats in their last three such outings against Porto (2-1), Vitoria de Guimaraes (5-0) and Santa Clara (2-0).

Only bottom-placed Estoril, who are yet to win a league match this season, have endured a longer winless run, while Maritimo have scored the third-fewest goals in the division (nine) and conceded the third-most (21).

Van der Gaag's men have also struggled to make home advantage count, recording just one victory from five league matches at their own ground and losing the last three, during which they conceded multiple goals on each occasion and scored just once.

Maritimo did, however, receive a welcome boost in the Taca de Portugal last weekend, progressing past Chaves following a goalless draw and a 3-2 penalty shootout victory, and will hope that result provides some momentum ahead of Friday's derby.

Nacional have also endured a difficult start to the campaign, but they have collected six points from their last three matches, including a 1-0 victory over Academico de Viseu courtesy of Matchoi Djalo's late winner.

That result marked the first victory under fresh boss Joao Henriques, who arrived in late October as the club's third permanent manager of the season following the departures of Joao Giao and Alexandre Santos.

Henriques initially struggled to build on interim coach Bruno Abreu's home victory over Braga, losing away to Arouca in his first match in charge, but the latest success has given the Alvinegros an opportunity to record consecutive competitive wins for the first time since beating Alverca and Tondela in April.

Interestingly, Nacional's last four matches have each produced just one goal, including their disappointing Taca de Portugal defeat to lower-division Sanjoanense on October 17, meaning taking maximum points on Friday could hinge on greater efficiency in attack and defensive discipline.

However, the Islanders still have plenty of room for improvement away from home, having collected just one point from five Primeira Liga trips this season, drawing at Santa Clara on the opening weekend before losing their next four against Vitoria, Sporting, Rio Ave and Arouca.

Nacional have also found this fixture difficult in recent meetings, losing four of their last five league encounters with Maritimo across the Primeira Liga and Liga 2 (D1), including a 3-1 defeat on their most recent competitive visit.

Maritimo form (all competitions):.

Nacional form (all competitions):.

Maritimo are monitoring defenders Rafael Fernandes (muscle) and Paulo Henrique (thigh), who both missed last weekend's cup tie against Chaves.

Yellu Santiago is also working his way back to full fitness from an injury, having only featured in the opening weekend of the Primeira Liga campaign.

Goncal Tabuaco's performance against Chaves has given Van der Gaag a decision to make in goal after he replaced Fran Vieites in the cup, saving two penalties during the shootout.

Nacional will be without Ulisses Wilson and Filipe Soares, who are both recovering from ankle injuries and remain unavailable.

Leo Santos (knee) is also sidelined, while Brazilian duo Wesley Gasolina and Liziero continue to recover from their respective injuries.

Henriques could retain the lineup that started against Viseu, with Miguel Baeza anchoring the midfield, although Djalo is pushing for a starting place after making an impact from the bench last time out.

Maritimo possible starting lineup:.

Vieites; Igor Juliao, Correia, Szalai; Tavares, Andrade, Guzzo, Ogbeta; Bassouamina, Butzke Tejon.

Nacional possible starting lineup:.

Industry News: Unconventional resistivity reduction in NbP semimetal nanoribbons

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5234 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that modern and future electronics harbour a key challenge: as conventional metal wires shrink to nanoscale dimensions, their resistivity increases sharply1 owing to surface and grain-boundary scattering.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that modern and future electronics harbour a key challenge: as conventional metal wires shrink to nanoscale dimensions, their resistivity increases sharply1 owing to surface and grain-boundary scattering. To circumvent this unwanted behaviour, here, we explore the fundamental limits of charge transport in topological semimetal niobium phosphide (NbP) nanoribbons down to approximately 6-nm widths, with industry-friendly top-down nanofabrication. The extracted NbP nanoribbon resistivity reaches 18 ± 4.1 μΩ cm at room temperature with an approximately 9-nm2 cross-sectional area, lower than that of conventional metals and semimetals with comparable size. The NbP nanoribbon resistivity decreases with decreasing width, unlike the classical behaviour of metals such as copper. This trend suggests a growing relative contribution of surface and edge states as the nanoribbon cross-section is reduced, despite a certain amount of disorder, including edge roughness. Our findings advance the understanding of size-dependent transport and scaling in this class of semimetals, offering a platform for nanoscale wires and interconnects in future nanoelectronics.
