a, High-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) image of the NbP (1.5 nm) nanoribbon with Nb (3.4 nm) seed layer. The electrically-conducting width of this device is ~12.5 nm. b, Magnified view of the nanocrystalline NbP layer and crystalline Nb seed, together with their corresponding Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), obtained from the boxed regions in panel a. c,d, Bright-field image (c) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental map (d) of the same device, showing distinct material compositions. In total, three NbP (1.5 nm) nanoribbons were examined by cross-sectional STEM. Across these samples, we observe consistent structural and compositional characteristics, including similar NbP crystallinity and sidewall oxidation, which support the scaling behaviour reported in this work. Additional STEM characterization was not performed on thicker NbP nanoribbons, as the thinnest nanoribbons are most relevant to the main conclusions of this study.

a, HAADF image of the NbP (1.5 nm)/Nb (3.4 nm) nanoribbon with an electrically-conducting width of ~18 nm. b, Magnified view of the nanocrystalline NbP layer and crystalline Nb seed layer, together with their corresponding FFT, obtained from the boxed regions. c,d, Bright-field image (c) and EDS elemental map (d) of the same device, showing distinct material compositions of each region. e, EELS linescan profiles of Nb (blue) and P (red) normalized intensity as a function of position along the direction indicated in panel c. f-h, Representative nanobeam electron diffraction (NBED) patterns extracted from 4D-STEM data at probe positions within the sapphire substrate (f), Nb layer (g), and NbP layer (h), with indexed reflections confirming the distinct crystal structure of each region. i-k, Orientation template matching of the representative NBED pattern in f–h, for the sapphire substrate (i), Nb layer (j) and NbP layer (k). Coloured symbols indicate the local crystallographic orientation of the best-matching template for that pattern. l-n, Phase template matching of the same patterns for the sapphire substrate (l), Nb layer (m) and NbP layer (n).

a, Schematic of the scaling mechanism for conventional metals, with surface scattering and grain boundary scattering. b, As thickness and width of NbP are reduced, the conduction is consistent with the growing dominance of surface carriers, which are disorder-tolerant, with reduced scattering. The total sheet conductance in this case is a sum of the sheet conductance contributed from bulk carriers and surface carriers. c, For thick NbP, bulk carriers dominate the transport, and thus conventional scaling laws apply, with pronounced surface and grain boundary scattering. d, The Fuchs-Sondheimer (FS) and Mayadas-Shatzkes (MS) model fitting of 3.4 nm Nb seed layer, showing an excellent fit. The extracted resistivity with increasing width (W → ∞) is 56.3 μΩ∙cm, which matches the literature results. e, Sheet conductance (GNbP,□) of 1.5 nm NbP as a function of width (red curve), extracted from Fig. 2d of the main text. The sheet conductance from bulk carriers (extracted from Hall measurement) follows the conventional FS-MS scaling model (black dashed line), where the sheet conductance from surface carriers increases as the width decreases due to the increased surface area/volume ratio, as indicated by the purple dashed line. At this ultrathin thickness (1.5 nm), bulk carriers experience strong scattering, resulting in very small bulk carrier sheet conductance. f, GNbP,□ of 10 nm NbP as a function of width (blue curve). At NbP thickness of 10 nm, 3D bulk carriers and 2D top and bottom surface carriers contribute comparably to transport, as shown in Fig. 4b. At this thickness, as the nanoribbon width is reduced, the enhancement in surface conduction is insufficient to offset the increased scattering of bulk carriers. Consequently, bulk transport dominates in this regime, leading to a net reduction of sheet conductance (i.e., increased resistivity) with decreasing width, more similar to conventional metal wires. We note that there could be subtle differences in sidewall roughness and damage in the thicker nanoribbons compared to the thinner ones. See Supplementary Note 2 for the modelling details and more discussion.

According to recent reports, a, Bulk Brillouin-zone schematic showing the two mirror planes and nodal rings from the band inversion. b, Representative band dispersion along Γ-S-M’, where the curves calculated without spin-orbit coupling (SOC) show the nodal-ring-related band inversion (plotted in green), and the curves calculated with SOC show the corresponding gap opening (black dashed lines). c, Real-space crystal view highlighting the helical states along the projected mirror line on the surface. d, Surface-state spectrum along \(\overline{\Gamma }\)-\(\overline{{\rm{X}}}\)-\(\overline{\Gamma }\)’, where the narrow Weyl-point window (grey shadow) hosts three pairs of helical states (indicated by arrows) that form the main part of the Fermi arcs, while remnant spin-split surface branches remain visible over a broader energy window (broad green shadow). Blue and red colours indicate the ‘± Sy’ spin polarization at opposite momenta, showing the helical feature. In summary, the narrow Fermi-arc structure is embedded inside a much broader nodal-ring-derived surface-state sector set by the band inversion. See Supplementary Note 7 for more discussion on bulk-topology hierarchy and topological surface-state interpretation.

a, Slab model along the [001] direction for the surface state calculations. Here, the 2 × 2 × 3 supercell is shown as an example. A 4.5 nm thick slab structure of the 1 × 1 × 4 supercell was used in the calculations. b,c, Surface band structures with Nb (b) and P (c) terminations along high-symmetry lines. Blue and red bands indicate the surface states of the Nb and P terminations, respectively. Bulk-projected states shown in pale blue are depicted as the background. The charge neutral point is set to 0 eV. d-f, Surface-projected Fermi surfaces with Nb (upper panels) and P (lower panels) terminations at 0 eV (d), −0.2 eV (e), and −0.4 eV (f). Darker colours represent larger contributions projected from the surface. Weyl points projected on the 2D Brillouin zone are shown as green and purple dots for opposite chirality. The constant energy cuts show surface-dominant open contours over a broad energy window, indicating that Weyl-derived surface bands persist even when the chemical potential is shifted deep into the hole-doped regime, which implies the robustness of the topological surface character. In addition, for the 4.5 nm thick NbP film, the top and bottom surface states exhibit minimal hybridization, except near the Weyl point projections where they meet each other. The Fermi-arc states remain largely unhybridized because they are well separated in momentum space. Even at momenta where they intersect, the resulting hybridization gap is negligible. See Supplementary Note 8 for the modelling details and more discussion.

According to recent reports, a, Slab model from the NbP (001) film with thickness d = 1.5 nm and width W = 4.4 to 5.7 nm. b, The one-dimensional (1D) band structure of a W = 5 nm nanoribbon along ky direction. The edge projection is highlighted in purple to show the edge states, while the bulk states are shown in pale blue. Near EF, the edge-projected subbands form an electron-like pocket, consistent with the negative pedge values (panel f). c-e, The spin projection to Sx (c), Sy (d), and Sz (e) components, respectively, for the edge state. The blue and red represent opposite signs of spin polarization. These edge states exhibit a pronounced spin texture arising from strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in noncentrosymmetric NbP where Sx and Sz components are locked to the ky momentum in a Rashba-type SOC. This reduces the wavefunction overlap between counter-propagating modes, thereby suppressing the leading backscattering channel, which indicates high-mobility edge conduction. f, The carrier densities from edge (pedge) and 2D film (p2D) are extracted from linear fitting of the total ribbon density (p1D) by p1D = pedge + p2DW, at varying W. Wc denotes the cross-over width at which the edge carrier density would dominate the transport over the top and bottom surface carrier density. Here, Wc ≈ 0 indicates that the enhanced edge conduction of ultrathin films is not primarily driven by an increased edge carrier density. Instead, it is more plausibly attributed to an enhanced carrier mobility arising from reduced backscattering as the edge dimension approaches the quasi-1D limit. See more details in Supplementary Notes 2 and 8. g, Agreement between the nanoribbon fitting (\({p}_{2{\rm{D}}}^{{\rm{NR}}}\)) and that obtained from independent slab film calculations (\({p}_{2{\rm{D}}}^{{\rm{slab}}}\)) which corresponds to the d = 1.5 nm thickness in Supplementary Fig. 10. This agreement supports the self-consistency of our calculations across both the nanoribbon and thin-film geometries.

Industry observers note that a, Temperature-dependent effective resistivity (ρeff) of NbP films with different thicknesses up to 90 nm, measured from Hall bar devices. These films have a 3.4 nm Nb seed layer, whose resistivity is measured separately (black symbols). b, Low-temperature limit (2-10 K) of panel a. The smallest superconducting transition temperature Tc (~2.2 K) is in the 3.4 nm Nb layer (black symbols), while higher Tc are observed in the NbP/Nb films, and Tc decreases monotonically with thicker NbP. The symbol colours follow the convention in panel a. c,d, Temperature-dependent sheet conductance (GNbP,□) (c) and resistivity (ρNbP) (d) for all NbP thicknesses, after subtracting the Nb seed contribution. e, ρNbP as a function of NbP thickness at 300 K and 10 K. For comparison, the ρNbP values of nanoribbons with the widest widths (Fig. 2d of the main text) are slightly higher than those from Hall measurements at 300 K, possibly due to process-induced damage during nanofabrication. f, Temperature-dependent ρeff of a ~5 nm-thick Nb control film, measured from a Hall bar device. The residual resistivity ratio (RRR) is 1.48, and the Tc is ~4.2 K. Inset: enlarged view of the low-temperature region. The presence of NbP appears to promote superconductivity in NbP/Nb films. The superconducting proximity effect is one plausible interpretation, although changes in disorder and enhanced inter-grain coupling (in the presence of NbP layer) could also contribute. We also cannot fully rule out the formation of an interfacial superconducting layer at the NbP/Nb interface. The NbP sheet conductance is obtained by subtracting the sheet conductance of the Nb layer (measured independently on control Nb films) from the total sheet conductance of the NbP/Nb stack. The extracted NbP resistivity is then obtained by dividing the NbP thickness by the NbP sheet conductance, i.e. ρNbP = dNbP/GNbP,□, where GNbP,□ = Gtot,□ - GNb,□ and Gtot,□ = dtot/ρeff, where Gtot,□ is the total sheet conductance of the NbP/Nb stack, dtot is the total stack thickness and ρeff is the measured effective resistivity (panel a). The GNbP,□ (panel c) represents the NbP sheet conductance after subtracting the independently-measured Nb seed contribution. Additional validation of the subtraction method using Pt/Nb stacks is provided in Supplementary Fig. 19. Control experiments using Pt/Nb stacks validate that the subtraction procedure itself does not generate an anomalous resistivity trend. Nevertheless, the conductance of the Nb seed layer within NbP/Nb stacks cannot be independently measured and it cannot be remarked, with absolute certainty, that its behaviour is identical to that of the separately measured Nb control film. Thus, the extracted NbP resistivity relies, by necessity, on the model used.

a-c, Hall resistance (Rxy) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at various temperatures for 3.4 nm Nb (a), 1.5 nm NbP (b), and 10 nm NbP (c). For the NbP films (b,c), the Nb seed layer contribution is subtracted at each corresponding temperature to extract NbP Hall response, using the same two-layer Hall conduction model described in the supplement. d, Effective three-dimensional carrier density (p3D) for all films, revealing opposite temperature-dependence: ultrathin 1.5 nm NbP shows an increasing p3D upon cooling, whereas both thicker NbP (10 nm) and Nb (3.4 nm) display decreasing p3D. (This figure is also included in the main text as Fig. 4d and is reproduced here for convenience). e, Effective hole mobility (μp) of the same films vs. temperature. NbP films exhibit a pronounced increase in mobility upon cooling due to suppressed phonon scattering, whereas the 3.4 nm Nb film shows only a slight rise in mobility, indicating that its transport remains strongly limited by surface scattering.

a-c, Longitudinal sheet resistance (Rxx) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at various temperatures for films of Nb seed layer (3.4 nm) (a), for NbP (1.5 nm) on the Nb seed (b), and for NbP (10 nm) on the Nb seed (c). All measurements were performed with the magnetic field applied perpendicular to the film plane and current direction. At low temperatures, all films exhibit a pronounced negative cusp near low field regions, arising from the interplay of superconducting fluctuations and weak antilocalization. d-e, Longitudinal sheet resistance (Rxx) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at 1.8 K for both 1.5 nm thick NbP (on 3.4 nm Nb seed layer) and for the Nb layer (3.4 nm) evaluated separately. Measurements were performed with B field perpendicular to the film plane and current direction (d), and with B applied in-plane (e). The superconducting transition temperatures are Tc ~ 6 K for the 1.5 nm NbP (on Nb) and ~2.2 K for the 3.4 nm Nb film (see Fig. 3d of the main text). The upper critical field Hc2, defined as the midpoint between the normal state resistance and zero resistance, is extracted. At 1.8 K, the out-of-plane critical field \({H}_{c2}^{\perp }\) is 2.2 T for NbP (1.5 nm) and 0.38 T for Nb (3.4 nm). The in-plane critical field at 1.8 K exceeds 9 T for NbP (1.5 nm) and reaches 4.44 T for Nb (3.4 nm). The superconducting coherence length estimates are provided in the supplement. The sense current used for Hall bar measurements is 0.5 mA, corresponding to a current density of ~0.1 MA/cm2 for the NbP (1.5 nm) film and ~0.15 MA/cm2 for the 3.4 nm Nb control, with the same 100 μm Hall bar device width. We note that this sense current is well below the superconducting critical current: even when we increased the sense current up to 10 mA, we were unable to suppress the superconducting state at 1.8 K.

The diffraction spots become progressively broader from layer 1 to layer 3, suggesting a gradual decrease in crystalline coherence in NbP layers further from the substrate. This is further supported by the emergence of diffuse ring features in the Layer 3 diffraction pattern, indicative of increasing structural disorder.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that luciano Spalletti will not hold his eve-of-match press conference before Sunday's trip to Fiorentina.
  • Juventus will travel to Florence without the usual preview from their coach.
  • The run began with a 2-0 win over Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on 1 November.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that luciano Spalletti will not hold his eve-of-match press conference before Sunday's trip to Fiorentina. Juventus arrive on two straight wins, chasing fourth place, against a coach Spalletti has never beaten.

Juventus will travel to Florence without the usual preview from their coach. Sunday’s game at the Franchi kicks off at 20:45. The squad got back to Turin overnight from the Netherlands. The reason given is the club’s crowded run of fixtures, TuttoJuve reported. It is the last game before the international break.

The run began with a 2-0 win over Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on 1 November. Kerim Alajbegovic scored in the 70th minute. Aged 19 years and 41 days, no foreign player had ever found the net at a younger age in a Serie A game between Juventus and Napoli.

Four days later, Juventus won 2-1 away at AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League. Teun Koopmeiners and Randal Kolo Muani scored. The result takes them to 10 points from four games in the competition. After the match, Spalletti described himself as very pleased with a solid team display against strong opponents. He felt his side should have added a third goal.

Recent findings suggest that the league position still needs work. The club’s stated aim this season is fourth place, and Como at the moment hold that spot. The defence gives some grounds for confidence. Going back to last March, no side can match the Bianconeri’s tally of 12 shutouts. Roma are next on 11.

It has been revealed that vanoli and Spalletti have faced each other only twice as coaches. Both meetings were Fiorentina-Juventus fixtures last season. Last November they drew 1-1 at the Franchi. Filip Kostic gave Juventus the lead before Rolando Mandragora equalised with a long-range shot.

The hosts’ struggles on their own pitch offer Juventus an opening against a side yet to find its footing at home.

According to recent reports, the fixture carries plenty of history. Sunday’s game is the 175th Serie A meeting between the sides, according to the club’s statistical preview. Juventus have won 82, Fiorentina 37, and 55 have ended level. Juventus have scored 275 top-flight goals against Fiorentina. Two more would draw them level with Inter’s 277, the highest total by any side against the Viola.

Once the international break is over, Juventus’s next Serie A match is on 22 November.

Tech Report: Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (680 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla owner Elon Musk remarked on Friday that the manufacturer would scale down production of the Cybertruck at its Austin factory in the coming year.
  • The South African entrepreneur stated Tesla would be scaling back production of his futuristic but often-mocked pickup truck and amping up production of what he hopes will soon become a fleet of fully automated taxis.
  • "Tesla will be winding down production of the cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk remarked on his X social media site.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla owner Elon Musk remarked on Friday that the manufacturer would scale down production of the Cybertruck at its Austin factory in the coming year.

The South African entrepreneur stated Tesla would be scaling back production of his futuristic but often-mocked pickup truck and amping up production of what he hopes will soon become a fleet of fully automated taxis.

"Tesla will be winding down production of the cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk remarked on his X social media site.

The announcement follows a bruising week for Musk amid the US midterm elections, where Republicans struggled despite his major donations, with his companies losing billions in value by market capitalization as investors sought to ditch stock.

Musk later responded to a complimentary user online who hailed the Cybertruck as the "best vehicle Tesla has ever made," and calling it an "end of an era" by saying: "True.".

For years he had poured much of his enthusiastic marketing zeal into promoting the Cybertruck, saying during the 2023 launch "finally, the future will look like the future.".

However the oversized body, straight lines and stainless steel and the post-apocalpytic vibe these created also met with widespread criticism and even mockery.

The electric powertrain was probably a barrier to sales in the US, by far the biggest pickup truck market, where Musk had hoped to take on some of the country's top-selling gas-guzzling vehicles like the Ford F150 or the Chevrolet Silverado and the Dodge Ram.

Meanwhile, the car's striking shape, weight and size made it impossible for Tesla to try to crack Europe, where electric vehicles are gaining a much larger market share.

Sources indicate that unlike in the US, EU safety regulations place considerable emphasis not just on people in cars in accidents, but also on the dangers posed to pedestrians who might be hit by a vehicle. That meant it was not possible for Tesla to register and sell the Cybertruck for road use in Europe.

Beyond this, the vehicle's size would likely have rendered it impractical and unpopular on many European roads, where space tends to be at more of a premium.

Depending how quick the wind-down proves to be, the Cybertruck's production run could prove shorter than its five-year R&D phase.

Given its longstanding issues meeting Musk's very public sales and production predictions, Tesla does not publish sales figures broken down by model.

But according to the automotive data platform Kelley Blue Book, the company sold 20,237 Cybertrucks in the US last year, down from 38,965 in 2024.

At launch in 2023, Musk had predicted unit sales nearer a quarter of a million.

In a recent development, for orientation, Ford sold more than 800,000 F-Series pickups in the US last year, a slight boost on 2024's numbers. These vehicles start at less than half the list price of a Cybertruck in the US.

In a recent development, the IPO for SpaceX this year revealed that Musk's second-largest tech giant was comfortably the biggest buyer of Cybertrucks in 2025. It bought vehicles worth $131 million and did not even enjoy a bulk-buy or friends-rate discount, paying list prices for the fleet.

The Cybercab is a vehicular element in Musk's bid to transform Tesla towards a company focused more on AI and robotics than automobilies.

Rather than just featuring the self-drive or driving assistance programs that Musk has been championing for years, the Cybercab has no steering wheels, pedals or mirrors at all and is designed never to have a human in control.

Musk say the model will be the organization's main autonomous model and will supply a global network of Robotaxis.

Starting in the past few months, around 300 such vehicles have been registered and have started operating, on approved roads in the Austin area near Tesla's Gigafactory Texas. They're being added to the existing fleet of autonomous Model Y Teslas being used for the purpose, serving in an area known as a geofence of around 680 square kilometers (264 square miles).

Champions League contenders PSG and Bayern Munich face contrasting attacking crises ahead of crucial tests

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1038 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 17:05.
  • Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich enter Wednesday's Champions League fixtures facing significant questions about their attacking strength, with injuries forcing Luis Enrique and Vincent Kompany to reconsider how their teams operate.
  • Industry observers note that the reigning European champions host Roma without Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, two of the players most responsible for providing individual creativity in Luis Enrique's fluid attacking system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 17:05.

Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich enter Wednesday's Champions League fixtures facing significant questions about their attacking strength, with injuries forcing Luis Enrique and Vincent Kompany to reconsider how their teams operate.

Industry observers note that the reigning European champions host Roma without Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, two of the players most responsible for providing individual creativity in Luis Enrique's fluid attacking system. Bayern, meanwhile, travel to Lille without Harry Kane, whose influence extends well beyond his remarkable goalscoring record.

Both clubs remain among the contenders for the European title, but the nature of their problems differs considerably. PSG must compensate for losing two players capable of creating advantages from wide positions, while Bayern are missing the central figure around whom much of their attacking play has been organised.

Their circumstances are also different in the league phase. Paris have won all four matches and collected 12 points, while Bayern sit 13th with eight points following two victories and two draws. Wednesday's matches will provide the first European examination of how both sides respond to their recent setbacks.

PSG's problems began on October 20, when Kvaratskhelia suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury during the 4-2 victory over Barcelona. The Georgian subsequently underwent surgery, leaving Luis Enrique without one of his most effective players in one-on-one situations.

The situation worsened on Saturday when Doue sustained a similar injury during the 3-2 Ligue 1 win at Nice. The France international had scored earlier in the match but was forced off before half time and now faces an extended recovery period.

The absence of both players removes two important sources of creativity from an attack built around movement, positional exchanges and the ability to beat defenders individually.

Kvaratskhelia's influence is particularly apparent on the left, where his dribbling and ability to move inside create space for overlapping teammates. Doue offers a different range of solutions, operating from the right while frequently drifting into central positions to combine with midfielders or attack the penalty area.

Losing both simultaneously could make PSG's attacking patterns easier for opponents to anticipate, particularly when facing teams prepared to defend in a compact shape.

Luis Enrique still has considerable resources. Ousmane Dembele is available after returning from a hamstring injury, while Maghnes Akliouche, Ferran Torres and Mika Godts provide options across the attacking line. However, finding an effective combination is likely to require more than simply replacing the two injured players with others occupying the same positions.

The Spaniard has nevertheless rejected suggestions that PSG must respond immediately in the transfer market.

"We don't need to sign players in the transfer window," Luis Enrique said ahead of the Roma encounter. "It's not our style to sign a player for just six months. We're happy with our squad.".

He also emphasised the resilience his team have demonstrated in recent seasons, insisting that the injuries would not diminish their ambitions.

Wednesday's meeting with Gian Piero Gasperini's Roma presents a particularly demanding test. The Italian coach favours aggressive defending and a flexible tactical approach, potentially challenging PSG's ability to progress through central areas without relying so heavily on their absent wingers.

Gasperini acknowledged the significance of the injuries but warned against underestimating Paris.

"PSG are a proper team and can also make up for the absences of very good players with their own organisation," he noted during his pre-match press conference.

For Luis Enrique, maintaining that collective identity while introducing new attacking combinations will be essential to PSG's hopes of challenging for a third successive European crown.

Bayern's immediate problem is concentrated through the middle of their attack, where Kane's absence has removed the team's most influential forward.

Sources indicate that the England captain suffered a syndesmosis ligament injury during Friday's 1-1 Bundesliga draw with Cologne and subsequently underwent surgery. He is expected to miss several months, depriving Kompany of a player who had already contributed 10 goals and 10 assists in 16 appearances this season.

Those figures illustrate the difficulty of replacing Kane. His value lies in his ability to drop into midfield, connect attacks and create space for teammates, as well as his finishing inside the penalty area.

A conventional replacement might occupy the same central position without providing the passing range and movement that allow Bayern's wide players to attack the spaces Kane creates.

Recent findings suggest that kompany's options have been further reduced by the absence of Ismael Saibari, who is recovering from an ankle injury, and Serge Gnabry. Michael Olise has also been ruled out of the Lille fixture with a foot problem, removing another significant source of creativity and attacking production.

There is some encouragement in the return of Luis Diaz, who is available again after a minor hamstring injury, while Jamal Musiala is working his way back towards full fitness. Neither development, however, eliminates the challenge of reorganising an attack that has relied heavily on Kane's contribution.

Bayern sporting director Max Eberl acknowledged that the team would need to adapt its approach.

"The dynamic of our play must change to an extent," Eberl told the club's official website. "We have to try with the team to defend well over the whole game and score the required goals.".

Kompany has similarly focused on the players available rather than those missing, describing the situation as exceptional but insisting that Bayern retain enough quality to compete.

In a recent development, "It's a chance to get wins in a different way," the Belgian said. "Now we have to show energy and mentality.".

Unlike PSG, Bayern have less room for error in the league-phase standings. Their eight points leave them outside the top eight places that guarantee direct qualification for the last 16, making the visit to Lille vital beyond its tactical implications.

Industry observers note that the two Champions League contenders therefore approach Wednesday with different priorities. PSG must preserve the variety of their wide attacking play, while Bayern need to establish a fresh way of creating and finishing chances without Kane.

The performances against Roma and Lille will offer an early indication of which adjustments are effective, although neither match alone can establish how the injuries will shape the remainder of their European campaigns.

Senegal KEEP Africa Cup of Nations title: Champions see crown restored in huge CAS verdict despite walking off the pitch in chaotic final against Morocco

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (789 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 09:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:47 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.
  • The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 09:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:47 EST, 24 November 2026.

Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.

The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.

Two months after the final, the CAF appeal board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match because their players had walked off the pitch in protest over a controversial penalty decision.

Morocco were subsequently awarded a 3-0 victory and the title. Despite that, Senegal refused to hand the trophy over.

That decision was based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which state that leaving the pitch constitutes a forfeit.

However, following an appeal to CAS, Senegal have been reinstalled as champions, with the court ruling that FIFA's law that the referee’s decision is final takes precedence over the competition regulations.

Therefore, because the officials did not enforce the competition regulations at the time, there were no grounds to overturn the result.

The Moroccan FA, though, have not given up and have vowed to take the matter beyond CAS after questioning the integrity of panelist Ulrich Haas.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has restored Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations winners after they were successful in their appeal.

Morocco were awarded a 3-0 victory two months after the final, after it was ruled Senegal had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch in protest over a late penalty decision.

Senegal fans clashed with security in Rabat after the controversial penalty decision.

Ruling in favour of Senegal on Tuesday, CAS mentioned: 'In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.

'As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the "field of play" doctrine.

'Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case.'.

A statement from the Moroccan FA later added: 'We take note of the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport regarding the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation against the decision of the CAF Appeals Committee, relating to the final match of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. In this context, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas (who sat on the CAS panel) and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

'The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and FIFA, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

'Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.'.

The chaos was triggered by events at the end of normal time, when referee Jean Jacques Ndala awarded Morocco a contentious penalty in the 98th minute after being called to the monitor by the video assistant referee to review El Hadji Malick Diouf’s challenge on Brahim Diaz.

The decision came just minutes after Senegal had seen a goal ruled out.

Furious with the penalty decision, Senegal manager Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest.

After a 17-minute delay, the team eventually returned, with former Liverpool forward Sadio Mane earning praise for remaining on the pitch and encouraging his teammates to continue.

In the dramatic aftermath, Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz saw his Panenka penalty stopped by Senegal goalkeeper Edouard Mendy, before Ndala brought normal time to an end.

Senegal went on to score early in extra time, which has now led to a second title in the past three editions of the tournament with their 1-0 victory eventually confirmed in the courtroom.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 17:29.
  • Manchester City's decision to wear a striking orange fourth kit during Tuesday's Champions League draw with Napoli has drawn criticism from supporter groups, while Premier League regulations mean the controversial shirt cannot be worn in domestic league matches.
  • Sources indicate that the Citizens abandoned their traditional sky-blue colours for the 2-2 encounter at the Etihad Stadium, unveiling a special-edition strip created by Puma and Italian fashion brand C.P.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 17:29.

Manchester City's decision to wear a striking orange fourth kit during Tuesday's Champions League draw with Napoli has drawn criticism from supporter groups, while Premier League regulations mean the controversial shirt cannot be worn in domestic league matches.

Sources indicate that the Citizens abandoned their traditional sky-blue colours for the 2-2 encounter at the Etihad Stadium, unveiling a special-edition strip created by Puma and Italian fashion brand C.P. Manufacturer. The launch formed part of a commercial collaboration, with the collection scheduled to go on sale worldwide on December 1.

Recent findings suggest that the decision proved divisive, particularly as Enzo Maresca's side extended their winless run to five matches. According to Brazilian outlet Trivela, two independent supporter organisations have questioned the timing of the initiative and its apparent prioritisation of commercial interests.

Recent findings suggest that there is also a regulatory complication. City have already registered their three regular kits for the 2026-27 Premier League campaign, meaning their newly introduced orange design cannot be added to the selection of strips available for league fixtures.

Premier League clubs are permitted to use a maximum of three registered outfield kits during a season, normally comprising their home, away and third-choice designs.

City have already filled those places with their traditional sky-blue home strip, a black-and-yellow away kit and a predominantly white third shirt featuring blue detailing.

Their latest orange shirt therefore falls outside the competition's permitted selection, regardless of whether the club wishes to use it again.

Industry observers note that the restriction is not related to the unusual colour, the shirt's design or its association with C.P. Organization. It follows from the fact that City have introduced an additional strip beyond the three registered for Premier League use.

UEFA's kit regulations operate differently, allowing clubs greater flexibility over the number of approved designs they can wear in European competition.

That explains why City were able to introduce the orange shirt against Napoli and could use it again during selected Champions League fixtures later this season.

The club confirmed the arrangement in an official statement following Tuesday's match, describing the outfit as a special-edition collaboration with Puma and C.P. Company.

Supporters will have an opportunity to purchase items from the collection at an exclusive pre-sale event at the City Store in Medlock Square on November 30, before the worldwide release the following day.

The FA Cup could also provide another opportunity to wear the shirt, although its use would require the appropriate approval from the Football Association.

It has been revealed that such exceptions are not unprecedented. Arsenal received permission to wear a special white kit in the FA Cup as part of their No More Red initiative, which raises awareness of knife crime and youth violence in London.

The Premier League restriction is only one aspect of the controversy surrounding City's latest release.

According to Trivela, the Citizens Trust, an independent supporter organisation established earlier this year, criticised the decision to introduce the orange shirt and expressed opposition to initiatives perceived as explicitly promoting third-party commercial interests.

Another independent organisation, the 1894 Group, reportedly raised concerns about the club's priorities, arguing that City should be concentrating on strengthening their relationship with supporters during a difficult period.

Those objections are particularly relevant because the fresh kit made its debut at the Etihad, where City would ordinarily wear their familiar sky-blue colours.

The orange design has no obvious connection to that traditional home identity. However, C.P. Tech giant has a longstanding association with British football terrace fashion, and its partnership with City dates back to 2024.

The club therefore has a cultural and commercial rationale for the collaboration, even if some supporters remain unconvinced by its appearance on the pitch.

Sources indicate that tuesday's result did little to improve the mood. City were held to a 2-2 draw by Napoli despite a late equaliser from Rayan Cherki, extending a difficult run for Maresca and his players.

The manager is already facing questions about his team's performances ahead of Sunday's Premier League trip to Arsenal, making the timing of a high-profile commercial launch a particularly sensitive issue.

City have previously demonstrated that fourth kits can generate interest without provoking the same debate over their relationship with the club's identity.

Their 2024-25 special-edition shirt, developed with Noel Gallagher, celebrated the 30th anniversary of Oasis's debut album, Definitely Maybe.

Industry observers note that the design drew on the Manchester band's history and Gallagher's longstanding support for City. It was worn during Champions League fixtures against Inter Milan and Paris Saint-Germain.

The latest collaboration follows a different approach, reflecting C.P. Firm's influence on football fashion rather than a specific event from the club's own history.

It has been revealed that there is no indication that City intend to withdraw the orange kit following the criticism. Their official announcement identifies it as an outfit for selected European fixtures, and the commercial launch remains scheduled for next week.

Recent findings suggest that for supporters attending Premier League matches, however, there will be no repeat of Tuesday's unusual appearance. City's three registered domestic kits will remain the available options, leaving the orange shirt as a feature of their European campaign.

Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1006 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Deeply indebted, politically trapped in a standoff between extremes and led by a government without a parliamentary majority: These are the defining features of France's current predicament.
  • If, in response to nationwide protests, the government plans to provide €4 billion ($4.48 billion) in low-interest loans to renovate schools by 2030 and allocate a further €1 billion to universities by 2029, it is promising money the state simply does not have.
  • France's public debt stands at around 120% of gross domestic product (GDP).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Deeply indebted, politically trapped in a standoff between extremes and led by a government without a parliamentary majority: These are the defining features of France's current predicament.

If, in response to nationwide protests, the government plans to provide €4 billion ($4.48 billion) in low-interest loans to renovate schools by 2030 and allocate a further €1 billion to universities by 2029, it is promising money the state simply does not have.

France's public debt stands at around 120% of gross domestic product (GDP). By comparison, Germany's debt-to-GDP ratio is roughly 65%, despite its €600 billion investment package for infrastructure and defense.

Recent findings suggest that germany still enjoys the highest possible AAA credit rating. France, by contrast, is rated AA, A+ or Aa3, depending on the credit agency. While Germany's outlook is consistently rated as stable, several agencies have assigned France a negative outlook.

In a recent development, as a result, the French government must pay higher interest rates on its borrowing than Berlin. The risk premium over German government bonds, known as the spread, is now at its highest level since the financial crisis. France pays nearly 1.6 percentage points more in interest than Germany on 10-year bonds.

The spread acts as a kind of "fever gauge" for bond markets, explained Friedrich Heinemann, an economist at the Leibniz Center for European Economic Research (ZEW) in Mannheim.

It has been revealed that "This fever gauge then forces a change of course. If the spread rises too sharply, France's financing conditions come under pressure, and anyone in France who needs a loan has to pay higher interest rates. Banks then get into trouble, and the crisis escalates further," Heinemann told DW.

"This could then slide toward a financial crisis, which would finally send a clear signal to everyone: Things cannot continue like this unless you are prepared to risk a genuine economic collapse," he said.

Landry Charrier, a researcher at the University of Bonn's Center for Advanced Security, Strategic and Integration Studies, however, does not expect France's debt-fueled spending spree to end anytime soon.

"French people are aware of the country's high public debt. But debt remains an abstract concept if its consequences are barely felt in everyday life. According to INSEE [the French national statistics agency — Editor's note], 56% of the population receive more in government benefits and services than they pay in taxes and social contributions. The majority therefore have a tangible interest in maintaining the status quo," Charrier told DW.

For more than half a century, France has regularly spent more than it collects in tax revenue. The last time it balanced its national budget was in 1974.

It has been revealed that france last paid a similarly high-risk premium at the end of 2011, during the eurozone debt crisis. What is particularly striking is how rapidly it has risen: Since June 2026, the spread over German government bonds has more than doubled.

Industry observers note that the main driver is not so much the general level of interest rates. Rather, it's the growing risk premium investors demand in response to high debt levels, political instability, large budget deficits and the recent unrest.

According to recent reports, the higher the interest rates, the larger the share of the national budget that must be devoted to debt servicing alone. France is expected to pay more than €79 billion in interest on its total public debt in 2026. That figure is projected to exceed €91 billion in 2027 and could reach between €125 billion and €132 billion by 2030.

Industry observers note that these figures include the costs incurred by social security funds and local authorities. The central government's interest bill alone is currently estimated at €62.6 billion by the Agence France Tresor, a French Treasury agency.

In the coming years, France will have to refinance large amounts of outstanding bonds that were issued when interest rates were at historic lows. At the same time, the country's substantial budget deficit means it must take on additional debt.

The trend of rising interest costs is also affecting Germany. The ZEW's Heinemann has calculated that German interest payments are likely to increase sharply by the early 2030s.

In a recent development, "For the federal government alone, which has so far paid around €30 billion, the figure will triple within a few years as both debt and interest rates rise. And it won't stop there — it will exceed €90 billion. Reaching €100 billion in annual interest payments in the federal budget is then no longer far off," warned the economist.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that in France, however, economic realities seem to have little impact on political debate. Both the far-right National Rally (RN) and the far-left France Unbowed (LFI) are campaigning on costly promises.

RN leader Marine Le Pen, for example, wants to reinstate the retirement age of 62 while promising €140 billion in savings. Jean-Luc Melenchon, LFI's leader, has even suggested that government bonds held by the French central bank should be "thrown into the fire.".

"Nobody will ever notice they've disappeared," he has claimed.

For Heinemann, this is "a good example of radical parties on both the right and the left simply telling economic fairy tales.".

Their common message, he said, is that "there is a way out of this mess that requires neither fiscal consolidation nor painful cuts.".

Charrier is convinced that many French people have yet to grasp the seriousness of the situation.

"The euro has made it easier for France to access cheap financing and has long softened the pressure to adjust," he pointed out.

In a recent development, "In the past, currency devaluations [of the French franc — Editor's note] made economic imbalances immediately felt through declining purchasing power and rising prices. Today, that warning signal is missing. This has created the illusion that necessary adjustments can be postponed indefinitely," Charrier noted.

This article was originally written in German.

By Joshua Cole | 25 Nov 2026 18:32.

Alanyaspor will be looking to halt their alarming slide down the Turkish Super Lig standings when they welcome Konyaspor to GAIN Park on Friday evening.

The hosts sit 14th in the table with 12 points from 12 matches, while the visitors occupy 15th place with eight points and will be hoping to close the gap after suffering three consecutive league defeats.

Alanyaspor have endured a difficult period in recent weeks, losing five consecutive league matches and leaving themselves increasingly vulnerable to being dragged into the relegation battle.

The Thunders began that sequence with a 3-0 defeat away to Fenerbahce before suffering a 2-1 home loss against Kocaelispor six days later, and their struggles continued when they travelled to face Genclerbirligi, suffering a humiliating 5-0 defeat, which was followed by a 2-0 home loss to Trabzonspor.

Those results led to Joao Pereira leaving by mutual agreement, with Ugur Ucar subsequently appointed, but the new manager was unable to bring about an immediate improvement as Alanyaspor were beaten 2-1 at Kasimpasa in his first game in charge.

They have now lost five Super Lig matches in a row and are without a win in their last six, drawing one, leaving Ucar with plenty to address as his side attempt to rediscover the form that helped them collect points earlier in the campaign.

Their recent performances have also been particularly disappointing defensively, having conceded 12 goals across their last five league matches, making them the worst-performing side in the division over that period.

The 4-1 victory over 12 Bingolspor in the Turkish Cup is the only positive result the Thunders have recorded during that spell, and just their second home win across all competitions, having won only their opening home league game, drawn two and lost two, leaving them without a league victory on home soil in their last four attempts.

However, Alanyaspor have enjoyed the better of recent meetings between the sides, remaining unbeaten in their last six competitive encounters with Konyaspor while winning each of the last five.

Konyaspor, meanwhile, have also struggled to maintain consistency this season and are four points behind the hosts, having collected just two wins, two draws and eight defeats from their opening 12 league matches.

Ilhan Palut's side have also lost their last three league games, suffering a heavy 4-0 home defeat against Galatasaray before losing 1-0 away to Samsunspor and then 4-2 against Besiktas in their latest outing.

Aside from their poor record in this fixture, the Anatolian Eagles have another concern heading into Friday's encounter, having collected just one point from five away matches this season.

In fact, Konyaspor have failed to score in their last four away matches, losing three of those games by a 1-0 scoreline, with a goalless draw against Kasimpasa coming between those defeats.

The Anatolian side have also failed to win on their last three visits to Alanyaspor, losing the previous two by 2-1 scorelines after drawing 2-2 on their earlier trip.

Ruan and Hwang Ui-jo are expected to feature in attack, while Ianis Hagi and Gaïus Makouta could provide creativity from midfield as Alanyaspor look to improve their scoring record.

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 15:24 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 16:26 EST, 24 November 2026.

Aston Villa made a miserable return to Istanbul as they wasted a wonderful opportunity to put one foot in the last 16 of the Champions League.

In a recent development, in the city that saw them lift the Europa League in May, Villa produced a limp display against a Galatasaray side missing star centre-forward Victor Osimhen. Villa failed to register a shot on target and are now without a win in six games in all competitions.

Substitute Deniz Gul headed the only goal 13 minutes from time as Villa boss Unai Emery cut an angry figure on the touchline and was booked late on. He also appeared to have a tense exchange with midfielder Ross Barkley.

Here Daily Mail Sport's TOM COLLOMOSSE looks at the key moments from another unconvincing Villa display.

Aston Villa left John McGinn out of the starting XI last Saturday and dropped two points in a drab 0-0 draw with Sunderland.

The skipper was back here but three minutes after he was taken off, Villa conceded. Careless defending at a corner allowed Gul to head home, though he took an accidental boot in the face from Nicolas Jackson that required lengthy treatment.

Unai Emery's decision to substitute John McGinn backfired as Aston Villa lost at Galatasaray.

Villa conceded three minutes after Emery decided to take off his captain (left) in Istanbul.

Deniz Gul scored the only goal of the game with a close-range header on Tuesday evening.

With McGinn on the field, Villa would surely have defended the corner better. Jackson's attempted clearance was poor and when the ball looped to Gul, others were too slow to spot the danger.

Industry observers note that mcGinn and Tyrone Mings are the leaders of this squad and in a period of such change, their role is more important than ever. Though Mings played here, he is no longer a regular starter.

While Emery's wish to protect McGinn is understandable, right now it is a luxury he cannot afford.

Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Harwood-Bellis 6, Lindelof 7, Mings 6, Maatsen 5; Kamara 7 (Buendia 82), J Gomes 6 (Goretzka 66, 6); Alysson 5 (Mbaye 66, 5), McGinn 7 (Barkley 74, 6), Manzambi 5 (Hemmings 74, 6); Jackson 5.

Booked: Jackson, McGinn, J Gomes, Emery.

It has been revealed that jackson has nine goals in 15 appearances for Aston Villa - but he has also picked up four yellow cards. Needless bookings proved the forward's downfall during his time at Chelsea and while he has been calmer at Villa, there is still work to do.

Recent findings suggest that during one clash in the first half with Gala defender Davinson Sanchez, Villa boss Unai Emery raced to the edge of his technical area to stop Jackson talking his way into the book. Emery succeeded that time, but not long afterwards, Jackson was punished for a needless tussle with Wilfried Singo.

Jackson plays on the edge. That is a major part of his game. He is also 26 next June and has enough experience to understand when to step into an argument and when to hold back. Emery does not count on Tammy Abraham much these days and Brian Madjo is raw, so he needs Jackson to keep his cool.

The Senegal forward was not the only one to test the patience of referee Daniel Siebert. Joao Gomes was lucky only to be booked for bringing down Yunus Akgun and then grabbing his opponent, while John McGinn was furious that Aleksey Batrakov escaped with a booking for appearing to kick out at the Villa skipper.

Nicolas Jackson's ill-discipline is a concern, with the striker having collected four yellow cards.

Recent findings suggest that for most of the last four years, any Villa fan could have written down Emery's first choice XI. Not these days, as Emery still seems to be searching for the ideal formula.

His uncertainty is understandable after losing five key outfield players in the summer but Villa's fortunes this season may depend on how swiftly Emery can make up his mind.

In a recent development, zion Suzuki is the clear first choice in goal and then of the 10 outfield players, how many are lock-ins? Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof in defence. Boubacar Kamara in the middle. John McGinn and - probably - Johan Manzambi in the three-man attacking line, and Nicolas Jackson as centre-forward.

That leaves four spots still up for grabs and not enough of those players are doing enough to convince Emery they deserve the shirt.

Latest Update: Germany hopes to host world ice hockey championship — without Russia

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (540 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A government spokesman has noted that, despite talks with the German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB), the International Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) and others, the impasse caused by last week's Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling remains.
  • Since the October 30 decision, several leading ice hockey nations — including Finland, Sweden and Czechia — have mentioned they would refrain from playing against Russia in any tournament in which it is allowed to take part.
  • The first tournament to be affected would be the Men's World Juniors, which opens in Canada in late December, followed by the IIHF's premier event, the Men's World Ice Championship, to be hosted by Germany in May.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A government spokesman has noted that, despite talks with the German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB), the International Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) and others, the impasse caused by last week's Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling remains.

Since the October 30 decision, several leading ice hockey nations — including Finland, Sweden and Czechia — have mentioned they would refrain from playing against Russia in any tournament in which it is allowed to take part. Several key sponsors have also threatened to pull out, should the Russians be allowed to play.

The first tournament to be affected would be the Men's World Juniors, which opens in Canada in late December, followed by the IIHF's premier event, the Men's World Ice Championship, to be hosted by Germany in May.

Stefan Kornelius, the spokesman for Germany's government, told reporters in Berlin on Friday that talks held with various stakeholders had made clear that Russia's participation would render the hosting of the championship "practically impossible — both from a sporting and an economic perspective.".

Kornelius mentioned talks would continue and the government still hoped for a diplomatic solution that would allow Germany to host the championship — as planned — in Gelsenkirchen, Mannheim and Düsseldorf in May.

"Our goal must be to hold the tournaments as scheduled," he said. "However, given the boycotts that would follow Russia's readmission, that would effectively be impossible. For this reason, we intend to explore — through dialogue — how we can still ensure the tournament takes place.".

Following the CAS ruling that the IIHF must allow Russia to return to international play, DEB chairman Frank Lutz had conceded that Germany may be forced to consider withdrawing as championship host.

Asked at Friday's press conference whether Germany could issue visas to a Russian team for the tournament, a Foreign Ministry spokesman declined to answer categorically, but did indicate that this would be difficult under restrictions currently in place.

"At a time when Russia is waging a war of aggression against Ukraine, there can be no 'normalcy' — and we will certainly not pretend that there is," remarked spokesperson Martin Giese.

Earlier this week, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney categorically ruled out Russian players taking part in the World Juniors in Alberta.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified ​war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," he said.

"So, ​if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors," he said, "the Russians will not be there.".

Russian President Vladimir Putin has also weighed in on the issue, accusing countries opposing Russia's return to international sport of violating the rights of his country's athletes.

The IIHF Council had originally called two days of meetings, on Monday and Tuesday, to try to reach a consensus on how to respond to the CAS decision — before extending discussions for a third day, on Thursday. By Friday, its members had evidently still not reached a consensus.

This comes as the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship, which is not affected by the CAS decision, opened in Denmark — and with the clock ticking toward the start of the World Juniors in Alberta on December 26.

Ekhator replaced McKennie in the 78th minute and Gatti came on for Lucumí in the 89th.

Breaking: As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond big promises?

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1232 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With its pulsing music, flashy images and barrage of special effects, the key message in Antalya's marketing video is clear: Turkey, the host of the 31st edition of the UN climate talks, is cool, stylish, modern — and eco-conscious.
  • Both President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his wife, Emine, make an appearance, with Turkey's first lady calling climate change "one of the most visible manifestations of the burden human activity has placed on our planet.".
  • In a recent development, from November 9-20, delegates from nearly every country in the world are coming together in the Mediterranean city of Antalya to chart a way out of the climate crisis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With its pulsing music, flashy images and barrage of special effects, the key message in Antalya's marketing video is clear: Turkey, the host of the 31st edition of the UN climate talks, is cool, stylish, modern — and eco-conscious.

Both President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his wife, Emine, make an appearance, with Turkey's first lady calling climate change "one of the most visible manifestations of the burden human activity has placed on our planet.".

In a recent development, from November 9-20, delegates from nearly every country in the world are coming together in the Mediterranean city of Antalya to chart a way out of the climate crisis. Turkey is the official host, and Australia will lead the negotiations. But the challenges they'll confront during those 12 days are far more serious than the showy marketing campaign make them out to be.

Severe drought, extreme heat, wildfires and record-low water levels in Europe's main waterways — summer across the continent was dominated by climate emergencies.

And in late August, a series of flash floods triggered by a rock-ice avalanche in Nepal and Tibet washed away entire villages, killing more than 1,400 people and leaving thousands missing. Climate experts have linked the disaster to melting ice and a warming climate.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Globally, carbon emissions are still rising: the UN has concluded that it is no longer possible to keep global temperature rise to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial levels, the goal agreed at COP21 in 2015.

According to recent reports, the global transition away from polluting fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas will be at the center of attention in Antalya — once again. To date, there's been no consensus on whether and how to transition rapidly away from this main source of global warming.

Despite the setbacks, the world has made some progress thanks to the 2015 Paris Agreement.

David Victor, a climate expert at the University of California San Diego, pointed out that before then, the planet was hurtling toward an average temperature rise of between 3-3.5 C.

It has been revealed that if current climate commitments are fully implemented, the latest UN projections show a rise of up to 2.6 C. It's a significant step forward, even though warming of that magnitude will still have worldwide consequences.

"There's no question that we could be doing more," stated Victor, though he cautioned against pinning too much on this year's summit.

Sources indicate that all agreements at COP need to be unanimous, meaning individual states can quash any sweeping resolutions. Added to that challenge are the ongoing wars, trade conflicts and other economic problems swirling around this year's negotiations.

Industry observers note that "It's like a giant Christmas tree in which everybody's hung their different ornaments, and the tree is groaning and more ornaments are being put on it," stated Victor. "We have to look at it for what it is: It's a place where people talk about stuff.".

Instead of waiting for all COP member states to agree, Victor sees a better chance for change in what he called "clubs" — smaller alliances of governments and companies working together to advance actual solutions, whether it be in aviation, shipping or electromobility.

Sources indicate that "The Paris process is vital. It has to go forward," he told DW. "But all the work is going to be done in clubs.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

An example of this approach was last April's first ever International Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels in Santa Marta, Colombia.

Colombia and the Netherlands invited representatives from 57 countries and key sectors to discuss ways to move the world away from coal, oil and gas, after an agreement on a similar blueprint failed at the 2025 climate summit due to opposition from several oil-producing states.

Industry observers note that with an eye to the ongoing trade conflicts and energy crisis, hosts Turkey and Australia have included green industrialization and the clean energy transition among their aims. One goal is to increase the share of electricity in global energy consumption to 35% by 2035, up from around 20% today.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

A recent analysis by the International Energy Agency found accelerating electrification could cut fuel-importing countries' energy bills by more than $400 billion (€357 billion) by 2035, compared to 2025 levels. The idea could appeal to regions dependent on fossil fuel imports — among them Germany and the European Union.

Ahead of COP31, German Environment Minister Carsten Schneider said Germany and the EU wanted to spark new momentum in the "global phaseout of fossil fuels.".

It's wouldn't just be good for the climate, but a chance for many countries to boost their economies and reduce dependence on energy imports, added Schneider in a statement.

According to recent reports, oil-producing states like Saudi Arabia, however, aren't interested in deals that will undermine their business model. At recent UN climate conferences, they've repeatedly blocked any final agreements, including phaseout aims.

Even China, despite its massive expansion of wind and solar energy over the last 20 years, could be against the idea. The economic superpower traditionally rejects any outside demands, proposals or interference concerning its national decisions on energy policy.

Every country in the world is affected by climate change, with loss and damage calculated in the hundreds of billions from heat, drought and storms. Worst hit are vulnerable countries in the Global South and island nations, who are at risk of disappearing as sea levels rise.

That's where money comes into play, with developing countries calling for more support to protect their citizens from the harms of global warming. At the 2024 UN climate talks in Baku, Azerbaijan, industrialized nations agreed to free up at least $300 billion annually in climate financing by 2035.

Recent findings suggest that but where exactly all those funds will come from remains hotly debated. At the same time, several major developed countries — most notably, the US — have cut their development aid.

The German government only paid out €4.7 billion from its 2025 budget for international climate financing, down from €6.1 billion in 2024.

"The level of financial support for developing countries today is far from what's needed," mentioned Jan Kowalzig, a climate expert at Oxfam Germany.

Breaking financial promises like this comes at the expense of losing the trust of developing countries and, as a result, the diplomatic power which Germany and other industrialized nations rely on to shape policy to fight climate change.

Cosima Cassel, who focuses on climate diplomacy at the independent think tank E3G in Berlin, believes Turkey's push to turbocharge electrification during an oil crisis could be successful.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

For Cassel, a successful outcome at what are expected to be difficult negotiations in Antalya would reveal actual political will behind the grand agreements.

When it comes to electrification, that means taking the expansion of electricity grids and battery storage capacity seriously — not to mention removing the barriers to further electrification.

In a recent development, manchester United transfer news: Red Devils captain Bruno Fernandes has turned down a second contract offer, according to a report from The Athletic covered by CaughtOffside. The 32-year-old is unhappy with both the proposed salary and the length of the deal, and the standoff lands with his current contract set to expire in June 2027.

The calendar adds pressure. In 50 days, Fernandes can open talks with foreign clubs, and Galatasaray have already been linked. United hold a 12-month extension option that stops him leaving for free, but triggering it only postpones the argument and keeps an unhappy captain in the dressing room.

Industry observers note that the refusal follows a bad few weeks. After a 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes publicly criticised Michael Carrick’s tactics, and Carrick dropped him for the Bournemouth game. Carrick has since been sacked with United 18th in the Premier League, inside the relegation zone, so Mauricio Pochettino inherits the standoff alongside a team in trouble.

His strengths are obvious. He set a Premier League record with 21 assists last season, delivers set pieces better than anyone at the club and opened this campaign with a hat-trick against Ipswich. His weaknesses are just as clear. At 32, the Portuguese international gives little protection when United lose the ball, and his shot selection can be wasteful.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino’s best sides pressed hard and ran through a creative number ten with two athletic midfielders behind him. Fernandes suits the creative role, but only if those two midfielders cover his space.

United should keep him, but on shorter terms than he wants. Nobody else in the squad creates chances at his rate, and a team sitting in the bottom three cannot replace that in January. A long, expensive deal for a player entering his mid-thirties would create a wage problem just as Pochettino tries to rebuild the midfield around younger runners.

Sources indicate that the sensible offer is a short contract with a raise tied to appearances and Champions League qualification. That respects his standing without committing United beyond the point where his legs start to fail.

If Fernandes still refuses, the board should trigger the extension and sell next summer. A sale with a year left on his deal will still bring a meaningful fee, whereas losing him for nothing in 2027 would waste the one asset United can sell on their own terms.

Last night, a report was published comparing the financials of AC Milan, Juventus and Inter and the findings are very interesting.

The big three bring a lot of attention to Italy and their footballing ecosystem, but that’s not all. Indeed, all three bring in vast amounts of money and have done so for years, which has helped them establish this dominance. However, their records last season show that a change could be on the way.

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, via Calciomercato.com, Inter recorded the highest revenue last season of €518 million, Juventus slotted in with €474.4m and then the Rossoneri finished ‘last’ with a revenue of €464.6m.

However, the profits – about that – of all three clubs didn’t line up in the same order. Inter recorded a €23m loss, then it was Milan with a €24m loss – largely helped by the summer signings – and Juventus finished last with a €66m loss.

Recent findings suggest that considering the Nerazzurri’s sporting successes in recent years, it makes sense why revenues are considerably higher, especially when looking at their Champions League records. For example, not being in Europe cost the Diavolo €54m between 2024/25 and 2025/26.

Sources indicate that in terms of squad cost, the Biaconeri were uncontested at the top, with a wage of €210m per season. Inter finished just below with €204m per season, whilst the Rossoneri ‘only’ spent €146m. Of course, this is still lucrative.

All in all, the foundations laid at Casa Milan are looking strong and if they can become more successful, their revenues could rocket up.
