📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 19:56.

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has offered a revealing assessment of his defensive hierarchy after substituting Eder Militao and Antonio Rudiger at half-time during Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV Eindhoven.

It has been revealed that los Blancos were trailing 1-0 at the Santiago Bernabeu when Mourinho made three changes at the interval, withdrawing both experienced centre-backs alongside Aurelien Tchouameni. Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen entered in defence, while Jude Bellingham replaced the French midfielder.

The decision preceded a remarkable turnaround. Madrid scored five unanswered goals in the second half, with Bellingham, Federico Valverde, Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Junior contributing to a victory that maintained their perfect Champions League record after five matches.

Although Mourinho insisted that the improvement was primarily down to a collective change in mentality, his explanation for replacing Militao and Rudiger offered an insight into why Konate and Huijsen have established themselves as his preferred central-defensive partnership.

The Portuguese coach acknowledged that the two younger defenders right now benefit from greater match sharpness, while identifying specific qualities that make them particularly valuable to his system.

Speaking to Movistar after the match, Mourinho explained that his decision had been influenced by several factors, including the yellow cards shown to Rudiger and Tchouameni during the opening period.

"A bit of everything," he remarked when asked whether the substitutions were motivated by fitness, disciplinary concerns or a desire to change the game.

"We had two players on yellow cards in a game against some very quick players, which was a risk.".

However, Mourinho's subsequent assessment was arguably more significant for the two defenders who had been withdrawn.

"Obviously, the two centre-backs who have been playing more regularly are in a better rhythm," he continued.

"Dean is our best player at bringing the ball out from the back, Konate is playing pretty well... and I thought those changes could help us.".

Those comments underline the advantages at the moment enjoyed by Huijsen and Konate, who have become Mourinho's regular pairing since the beginning of the campaign.

Huijsen's ability to progress possession from defence is particularly crucial in a Madrid side expected to dominate the ball, while Konate provides the physical presence and defensive intensity required when the team presses high.

Both qualities were evident in the second half against PSV, when Madrid pushed their defensive line forward and prevented the Dutch visitors from progressing comfortably through midfield.

Mourinho nevertheless resisted the suggestion that his defensive substitutions alone had transformed the contest.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United manager also credited Bellingham's introduction and a collective improvement in pressing, explaining that his players had struggled to win individual battles before the interval.

Industry observers note that "The second half was a question of mentality," Mourinho remarked. "We made changes, yes, and Jude is a different kind of player who gives us what we lacked in the first half, but collectively we were better in the second half.".

According to recent reports, his explanation makes it difficult to interpret the removal of Militao and Rudiger as an outright rejection of either player. Yet publicly highlighting the superior rhythm and individual qualities of their competitors offers a clear indication of the current pecking order.

The situation is particularly delicate for Rudiger, whose contract expires in June 2027.

The 33-year-old German has found regular opportunities difficult to secure under Mourinho, and reports in Spain have suggested that Real Madrid are increasingly unlikely to offer him another extension.

His experience remains an asset, particularly across a demanding season involving several competitions, but his reduced role raises questions about whether he will remain at the Bernabeu beyond next summer.

Militao faces a different challenge.

The Brazil international remains under contract until June 2028, although his recent career has been disrupted by two serious anterior cruciate ligament injuries and further muscular problems.

He has played only five minutes in La Liga this season, with his Champions League appearances providing most of his opportunities to regain competitive sharpness.

Tuesday's meeting with PSV represented another chance to demonstrate his readiness for a more prominent role. Instead, his involvement ended after 45 minutes as Mourinho turned to the partnership that has largely carried Madrid's defence this season.

Recent findings suggest that the Brazilian's limited playing time makes the manager's comments about rhythm particularly relevant. Regaining his previous level requires regular appearances, but those opportunities are difficult to obtain while Konate and Huijsen continue to perform.

Huijsen's emergence has already complicated Militao's attempts to recover a starting place, with the Spain international establishing himself as a central figure in Mourinho's defensive prepares.

Konate, meanwhile, has made a strong impression following his arrival from Liverpool, offering the combination of athleticism and defensive aggression that the Portuguese coach values.

The two established internationals therefore face different uncertainties. Rudiger must consider his future as his contract approaches its conclusion, while Militao has more time remaining on his deal but needs to demonstrate that he can compete consistently for a starting position.

Mourinho has not announced plans to sell either defender, and Tuesday's substitutions should not be regarded as confirmation of their departures.

However, the manager's unusually explicit assessment of his centre-backs has reinforced the challenge facing both players: Konate and Huijsen currently possess the match rhythm, tactical qualities and established partnership that make them difficult to displace.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Surveys show that only a minority of respondents report feeling a strong sense of community between those from former East and West Germany, and many continue to perceive significant differences.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When the Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, ending East Germany's isolation from the West, the event was celebrated on both sides of the border. Yet, 37 years later, many people on both sides remain deeply skeptical of each other.

Surveys show that only a minority of respondents report feeling a strong sense of community between those from former East and West Germany, and many continue to perceive significant differences.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

We asked three artists from Germany with different perspectives on the history of the country's division to share their views.

Author Lea Streisand was born in 1979 and experienced the fall of the Berlin Wall firsthand while growing up in East Berlin.

In her books and essays, she has returned to her East German upbringing many times, using literature to process it.

The novel "Hufeland, at the corner of Bötzow" (2019, Ullstein), for example, recounts the period of reunification from a child's perspective.

According to recent reports, "November 9, 1989, was simply incredible," she told DW. She was 10 years old at the time. When her mother bought her winter boots with the 100 Deutsche Marks she received from the West German state — a welcome gift given to all East German citizens — she was so disappointed that she felt like crying. But later, a friend of her parents' let her buy so many sweets at the supermarket that they lasted until Christmas.

Industry observers note that "The disappointment really set in afterwards, with what happened over the course of the following year. It was unbelievable how rapidly an entire system was suddenly swept away and a latest one built up, as if to say, 'There you go. You're welcome'," Streisand recalled. "I think it was just too fast for people.".

It has been revealed that the people of East Germany, or the GDR, had brought about the fall of the Berlin Wall themselves through a civil rights movement and numerous demonstrations. For many, however, the goal was not to dissolve the state immediately but to reform it.

Recent findings suggest that among them was Anke Feuchtenberger, born in 1963 in East Berlin. Her childhood was spent in East Berlin and in the East German region of Western Pomerania, where she now lives again and feels "very much at home.".

Industry observers note that today, she teaches at the University of Applied Sciences in Hamburg, meaning she spends time on both sides of the former divide. Feuchtenberger is often described as Germany's most influential comic artist. Her work has also garnered international acclaim.

"Back then, as artists, we tried to bring about a change through posters and flyers — to gain more freedom without immediately abolishing socialism," she explained.

In a recent development, at the time, the fall of the Berlin Wall stirred up mixed feelings in Feuchtenberger: "I soon realized that the creative and revolutionary aspects of our movement were very rapidly being smothered by consumerism, and that nationalist tendencies — which had already been noticeable before — were coming to the fore," Feuchtenberger recalled. "That made me afraid.".

According to recent reports, meanwhile, for photographic artist Simon Menner, born in 1978 in Emmendingen, in the West German state of Baden-Württemberg, Berlin was very far away. As Menner put it, he experienced the fall of the Berlin Wall as a child in a "rather abstract" way. Today, Berlin is his home.

In his experience, the way films and documentaries portrayed East Germany around the time of reunification was very bleak. "But West Germany in the '80s," he mentioned, "was also bleak and very staid.".

This uneven portrayal of the two parts of Germany is an glitch that deeply concerns Menner — partly because he unwittingly contributed to it in a small way. Among other things, Menner's work explores the topic of surveillance and how it works.

In the archives of East Germany's Ministry for State Security, or Stasi — which are freely accessible today as part of the National Archives — he discovered a massive collection of photographs that both fascinated and horrified him and which he wanted to bring to the attention of a wider public.

His photo book "Top Secret" (2012, from publisher Hatje Cantz) features a selection of photos that offer a unique insight into the work of the Stasi. Some are eerie, while others are curious or even absurd.

Sources indicate that menner also tried to look into the photo archive of West Germany's Federal Intelligence Service. "I spent a year trying to gain access — without success," he said.

In hindsight, he now finds his artistic project problematic because he believes it is too one-sided, focusing exclusively on East Germany's past.

In a recent development, according to Menner, West Germany's intelligence services in the 1960s were not exactly models of virtue either, and he believes it is "actually high time" to critically examine this part of history as well. In his view, an honest examination of Germany's past as a whole is a prerequisite for genuine reconciliation.

Recent findings suggest that streisand believes literature can help foster mutual understanding. "Literature opens a window into experiences we haven't had ourselves," she stated. "You can immerse yourself in the mind of someone who has had a different life than you have and understand what happened.".

Interest in these stories remains strong. In 2023, Feuchtenberger published the nearly 500-page graphic novel "Comrade Cuckoo" (published by Reprodukt), which was the first graphic novel to be nominated for the Leipzig Book Fair Prize in the fiction category.

According to recent reports, the story spans a childhood in the fictional East German village of Pritschitanow in the 1960s in the GDR to the post-Reunification era. In it, Feuchtenberger weaves autobiographical memories of her upbringing with fantastical and fictional elements.

The artist noted she was surprised "that, so long after the fall of the wall, my stories have sparked such great interest in the West.".

In particular, the fact that the main character, Kerstin, rarely sees her parents because they both work full-time is a topic that often comes up at readings. In the GDR, everyone had the right to work, she said. At the same time, it was a civic duty.

According to recent reports, could the West German interest in this stem from the fact that full-time employment for both parents has long been less common in the West? It's possible, remarked Feuchtenberger.

When looking toward their shared future, the two East German women are more optimistic than Menner, from West Germany.

In a recent development, "In Berlin, I often don't even notice anymore whether I'm in the West or the East," mentioned Menner. "But when it comes to sociopolitical issues, politicians should listen to older and younger people more closely," he added, referring to the recent election successes of far-right Alternative for Germany, or AfD . "Otherwise, things are going to get difficult in the near future.".

"It's very important to step outside our own bubble because people all over the world are facing problems. Constantly focusing on this German-German divide that has emerged between the groups doesn't help," said Feuchtenberger.

In a recent development, "For me personally, the whole issue of borders has somehow dissolved," she explained. This is due in no small part to the many trips abroad that have taken her to various places around the world.

Moreover, in her hometown near the Polish border, she observes how animals couldn't care less about the border. "They come from the east and the west and do whatever they want," she stated. That's why she also gave "Comrade Cuckoo" the working title "A German Animal in a German Forest," "because I found the absurdity of an animal having a nationality so funny.".

In a recent development, "This East-West thing — our children won't have any interest in it at all," remarked Streisand. "Young people don't care where their parents come from. Can I get a job that will support a family? Do I have to go to war? Right now, completely different things are relevant.".

An extremophile transgene improves drought resistance and yield in cereals

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 120 min read (24038 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~120 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production1,2.
  • According to recent reports, the bulk of crop production worldwide strictly depends on rainfall to support irrigation needs, and limitations on water availability pose a global challenge for agricultural productivity, with water scarcity and drought stress incurring unpredictable and potentially catastrophic effects on yield1,2.
  • Conventional plant-breeding efforts have boosted crop yields in water-limited environments, for example, through improved stress resistance, greater biomass accumulation, delayed leaf senescence or ‘stay-green’ strategies7,10, but broad potential remains for improving yield and yield stability across growing regions regardless of water availability11,12.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production1,2. On average, crop productivity typically declines by 30–40% in moderate-drought years, whereas extreme droughts trigger far greater reductions3,4. As droughts become longer and more intense due to climate change, adverse effects on crop productivity are expected to escalate5. Breaking the trade-offs between stress resistance and yield is key to advancing crop genetic improvement as climate change sets in and the world population grows, but this is challenging for drought stress6. Here we show that heterologous expression of EpTFIIAγ, a gene encoding a transcription factor induced by osmotic stress in an extremophile lichen mycobiont, partially decouples trade-offs between stress resistance and grain production, enhancing plot yields of five wheat cultivars under water deficit by 19.4–32.8%, and per-plant yields of rice and maize by 19.7–42.4% in the greenhouse and multiple field environments. EpTFIIAγ physically interacts with endogenous transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance both stress-responsive and developmental transcriptional programs, simultaneously boosting photosynthetic capacity and water-use efficiency, while delaying senescence via multiple physiological and developmental enhancements, ultimately increasing grain yields. EpTFIIAγ uncouples antagonistic stress-response and biomass production pathways in multiple crops and delivers a straightforwards and broad-spectrum strategy for sustainably improving staple-crop yields regardless of water availability.

According to recent reports, the bulk of crop production worldwide strictly depends on rainfall to support irrigation needs, and limitations on water availability pose a global challenge for agricultural productivity, with water scarcity and drought stress incurring unpredictable and potentially catastrophic effects on yield1,2. The adverse effects of climate change on crop productivity have historically been underestimated5. With the average global temperature expected to increase by 1.5–2.0 °C by 2050, the frequency and severity of drought events will be further increased, which could be accompanied by 30–40% reductions in food production3,4. Despite facing the greatest food-security challenges in the modern era7,8, annual crop yield improvement rates have not kept pace with projected food demands, that is, a 50–70% increase to accommodate approximately 9.8 billion people worldwide by 2050 (ref. 9), further compounding the effects of disaster events and decreasing availability of arable land.

Conventional plant-breeding efforts have boosted crop yields in water-limited environments, for example, through improved stress resistance, greater biomass accumulation, delayed leaf senescence or ‘stay-green’ strategies7,10, but broad potential remains for improving yield and yield stability across growing regions regardless of water availability11,12. Increasingly precise genetic modification strategies have advanced crop engineering for drought resistance13,14,15,16,17. For example, heterologous expression of a rice trehalose-6-phosphate phosphatase in developing maize ears improves yield under both well-watered and drought-stress conditions in the field16. In cassava, expressing a modified Arabidopsis potassium (K+) channel in vascular tissues improves K+ transport, photosynthesis and root biomass, allowing enhanced productivity in nutrient-poor and drought-prone environments17. However, genetic modification usually cannot provide a single, universal solution to multifactorial drought stress, and this approach frequently fails to improve yields in the field13,18 because drought resistance is a complex quantitative trait involving a multitude of small-effect loci or genes mediating diverse stress responses, such as stomatal closure (for reduced transpiration) or modified root architecture (for enhanced water uptake)10,19. Drought resistance typically accompanies trade-offs by way of reduced yield in the absence of stress6,20, undermining the effectiveness of certain genetic modification strategies. Therefore, of the genes identified in controlled conditions that often show limited effects in real-world environments, relatively few undergo rigorous field trials to properly demonstrate consistent agronomic value21.

Among known genetic resources for drought resistance, lichens have been generally overlooked despite their ubiquitous distribution across extreme ecological niches. In arid-adapted lichens, mycobionts appear to contribute more to survival under water deficit than photobionts22,23. We have previously isolated the lichen-forming fungus Endocarpon pusillum, which has extreme drought resistance. Exposure to dehydration stress identified 1,781 differentially expressed E. pusillum genes24. Through mining those data, here we identified the transcription factor gene EpTFIIAγ that broadly enhances yield and biomass production under field conditions when heterologously expressed in the world’s top-three-produced staple cereal crops of bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.), maize (Zea mays L.) and rice (Oryza sativa L.). EpTFIIAγ delays plant senescence, enhances photosynthetic capacity, water-use efficiency (WUE) and drought resistance by functioning as a transcriptional co-factor to coordinately target multiple genes and pathways. EpTFIIAγ binds to TATA-box-containing motifs and interacts with several endogenous wheat transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance networks involved in stress responses, plant development, photosynthesis and grain yield. Our results provide an unprecedented broad-spectrum resource for crop improvement and highlight the untapped potential of lichen mycobionts as sources of versatile transgenes for biotechnology.

Among 25 differentially expressed genes predicted to encode transcription factors identified under dehydration stress in E. pusillum (Fig. 1a), EPUS02736 exhibits the strongest upregulation and encodes a transcription initiation factor IIA γ-chain (designated EpTFIIAγ). EpTFIIAγ shares homology with TFIIAs from plants, such as Arabidopsis, wheat, rice and maize, although the genetic relatedness between EpTFIIAγ and these homologues is relatively distant (Fig. 1b). Strong expression under dehydration stress implicates EpTFIIAγ in drought adaptation of the lichen mycobiont. Towards understanding its functionality, EpTFIIAγ was expressed in the yeast ∆hog1 mutant (deficient in HOG1, which encodes the high osmolarity glycerol 1 protein kinase), resulting in remarkably enhanced growth on solid synthetic dropout (SD) −Ura medium with 0.75 M sorbitol (Fig. 1c), and statistically significantly higher growth in corresponding liquid medium than the control (Fig. 1d). These results suggested that EpTFIIAγ contributes to regulating osmotic stress.

It has been revealed that to determine whether EpTFIIAγ could also enhance drought resistance in plants, we first expressed endogenous TFIIAγ genes from Arabidopsis and wheat in the yeast hog1 mutant; however, no obvious effect on osmotic stress tolerance was observed (Fig. 1c), suggesting that TFIIAγ genes probably mediate divergent biological functions between plants and E. pusillum. We then generated three genetically independent transgenic Arabidopsis lines (TL1–TL3) constitutively and heterologously expressing EpTFIIAγ and examined drought resistance. To our surprise, seedlings expressing EpTFIIAγ had survival rates approximately seven times higher than wild-type Col-0 controls under drought-stress conditions (Fig. 1e). This improved drought resistance was not limited to the eudicot Arabidopsis. Transgenic wheat cv. Fielder seedlings heterologously expressing EpTFIIAγ from the strong and constitutive Ubiquitin promoter showed an approximately 3.5-fold increase in survival rate compared with wild-type Fielder under drought stress (Fig. 1f). However, overexpression of endogenous AtTFIIAγ or TaTFIIAγ in their respective native hosts had no such positive effect on drought resistance (Extended Data Fig. 1a–f), supporting their functional divergence from EpTFIIAγ. Analysis of key drought-resistance traits, including root architecture and biomass production (Extended Data Fig. 1g–o), stomatal density and aperture, and leaf water loss and transpiration (that is, leaf temperature; Extended Data Fig. 1p–u and Supplementary Fig. 1), suggested that the enhanced drought resistance among EpTFIIAγ transgenic Arabidopsis and wheat lines was mainly attributable to enhanced root growth and decreased stomatal aperture and transpiration compared with wild-type controls. Transgenic EpTFIIAγ wheat seedlings over-accumulated abscisic acid, auxin and salicylic acid hormones than wild-type Fielder plants under drought stress, whereas their accumulation remained comparable with that of controls under well-watered conditions (Supplementary Fig. 2).

Sources indicate that drought resistance varies widely across wheat germplasm25. To understand whether EpTFIIAγ can endow major commercially relevant wheat cultivars in China with enhanced drought resistance, we generated four genetically independent transgenic EpTFIIAγ lines in each of cvs. Xinong979 (XN979), Xinong511 (XN511), Jimai22 (JM22) and Xingzi9104 (XZ9104), which show different degrees of stress resistance and yield25,26. Greenhouse drought-resistance assays revealed that survival rates were 2–3 times higher for transgenic lines than corresponding wild-type controls (Fig. 1g–j), whereas stomatal aperture, leaf water loss rates and transpiration were also decreased in transgenic lines under drought stress (Supplementary Figs. 3 and 4). Therefore, heterologous EpTFIIAγ expression consistently endowed drought resistance and key physiological changes across four additional wheat cultivars. EpTFIIAγ plants also displayed broad-spectrum resilience to heat stress, lodging and multiple races of the major wheat stripe-rust fungal pathogen Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici (Extended Data Fig. 2), further supporting potential EpTFIIAγ deployment for engineering stacked resistance to environmental stressors in wheat.

Sources indicate that certain transgenes are known to improve resistance to drought stress but at the undesirable expense of reduced plant growth or productivity, known as yield drag13,18,20. We examined performance of all five sets of transgenic EpTFIIAγ wheat lines to identify potential yield drag in 3-year field trials under full-irrigation and water-limited conditions with a rain shelter in Yangling, China, which is characterized by a warm temperate semi-humid and semi-arid climate with 200–400 mm of rainfall during the growing season (Supplementary Fig. 5). All tested EpTFIIAγ lines had consistently increased grain yield across different genetic backgrounds and years compared with respective wild-type controls under full-irrigation control conditions. This increase was more pronounced under water-limited conditions (Fig. 1k–n; Supplementary Tables 1–3 and Supplementary Figs. 6–9). In 2025, grain yields surpassed that of the two previous years under water-limited conditions for EpTFIIAγ lines because of the higher temperature, lower rainfall and severe drought stress (Supplementary Fig. 5). Across all five backgrounds, EpTFIIAγ lines displayed 7.6–13.9% increases in grain yield per plant and 7.9–13.5% increases in yield per plot relative to controls under full-irrigation conditions, and increases of 22.3–38.3% in yield per plant and 19.4–32.8% higher yield per plot under water-limited conditions (Fig. 1m,n, Supplementary Tables 1–3 and Supplementary Fig. 7c,i). EpTFIIAγ lines were taller, had increased plant biomass, grain length, grain width and grain weight relative to respective wild-type controls, potentially contributing to increased plot yields. Despite higher grain yields, EpTFIIAγ plants had similar straw weight compared with wild-type plants, resulting in 6.1–14.8% higher harvest indices (that is, ratio of grain yield to aboveground biomass) under full irrigation and 7.6–15.5% increases in harvest indices under water-limited conditions (Supplementary Tables 1–3 and Supplementary Figs. 6 and 7). Growth duration was similar between genotypes under full irrigation, whereas time to maturity was 2–5 days longer for EpTFIIAγ transgenic lines than maturation time in the wild-type under water-limited conditions (Supplementary Fig. 7f,l), reflecting adaptation to drought stress.

Sources indicate that to evaluate trait stability, additional field trials were conducted in 2025 in three arid growing regions in China (Heyang, Shaanxi; Linfen, Shanxi; and Cangzhou, Hebei) with rainfall of 120–250 mm during the growing season. Grain yield per plant for EpTFIIAγ lines increased by 10.9–25.6% compared with wild-type controls, with the highest yield increases (15.6–25.6%) observed in Heyang (Supplementary Tables 4–6). These results underscored the potential of EpTFIIAγ as a valuable genetic resource for developing drought-resistant, high-yield wheat varieties in elite backgrounds regardless of water availability. In detail, EpTFIIAγ plants had expanded flag leaves, accelerated grain filling, larger pericarp cells, higher starch granule density and increased starch biosynthesis relative to wild-type controls under both full-irrigation and water-limited conditions (Extended Data Fig. 3 and Supplementary Fig. 10). This accelerated filling led to heavier grains beginning at 5 days after flowering, regardless of water conditions, resulting in 3.3–8.8% greater final grain weight in well-watered EpTFIIAγ plants and 15.2–21.4% higher grain weight in drought-stressed transgenic plants than in their respective wild-type controls (Fig. 1m,n, Supplementary Tables 1–3 and Supplementary Figs. 6 and 7). These improvements were consistent with the higher sucrose, glucose and fructose levels, as well as increased sucrose synthase, cell-wall invertase and ADP-glucose pyrophosphorylase activities observed in EpTFIIAγ grains during the early filling stage (Extended Data Fig. 4). Conversely, flag-leaf sheaths of EpTFIIAγ plants had lower levels of these sugars than wild-type controls. These results suggested that the extended duration and enhanced rate of grain filling may be key determinants of increased final grain weight and yield in EpTFIIAγ plants.

It has been revealed that given the drought resistance and yield boosts endowed by EpTFIIAγ in transgenic wheat lines, we examined which physiological processes are altered. EpTFIIAγ plants had delayed senescence compared with controls under water-limited conditions (Supplementary Figs. 8 and 9), which we hypothesized might be due to increased WUE. We also hypothesised that carbon assimilation might be altered given that increases in yield and biomass require enhanced carbon fixation. To examine possible differences in water status and carbon assimilation between wild-type Fielder and EpTFIIAγ plants, we first used plant multispectral imaging to estimate normalized difference vegetation index and normalized water index values at seedling stage in a growth chamber. Transgenic plants indeed had higher normalized difference vegetation index and lower normalized water index values than Fielder plants under both well-watered and drought-stress conditions (Supplementary Fig. 11). EpTFIIAγ seedling leaves had lower 13C fractionation than Fielder during the 18 days of drought treatment following water withdrawal (Fig. 2a), indicating enhanced WUE in these transgenic plants. These results are consistent with the lower water loss rate and transpiration for EpTFIIAγ plants under drought-stress conditions (Extended Data Fig. 1p–u).

To further assess the effects of EpTFIIAγ expression on carbon assimilation, we measured quantum yield of photosystem II photochemistry (ΦPSII). Transgenic EpTFIIAγ seedlings had approximately 14.6% higher ΦPSII than Fielder control plants under well-watered conditions, and approximately 29.9% greater ΦPSII under drought stress (Extended Data Fig. 5a,b). These results suggested that EpTFIIAγ expression led to enhanced maintenance of PSII activity. EpTFIIAγ plants had improved light–response and CO2–response curves of net photosynthesis (Fig. 2b,c). In addition, the abundance of PSI, PSII, cytochrome b6/f and LHC proteins, as well as RuBisCO subunits were all increased in transgenic plants under well-watered or drought-stress conditions (Extended Data Fig. 5d). RuBisCO activity was increased in EpTFIIAγ plants (Extended Data Fig. 5c), which agreed with A–Ci curves showing higher maximum rates of RuBisCO carboxylation and electron transport (Extended Data Fig. 5e–h). Consistent with these increases, EpTFIIAγ leaves over-accumulated sucrose, glucose, starch and soluble sugars (Extended Data Fig. 5i), further demonstrating enhanced carbon assimilation in these plants. Of note, drought stress triggered a marked accumulation of root soluble sugars (for example, sucrose, glucose and fructose) in EpTFIIAγ plants compared with Fielder, whereas no such difference was observed under optimal conditions (Extended Data Fig. 5j), aligning with enhanced root growth under drought stress.

We next evaluated how EpTFIIAγ contributes to lifting photosynthetic capacity in field-grown plants. Chlorophyll content (soil and plant analyser development, SPAD), maximum quantum yield of PSII photochemistry (Fv/Fm) and photosynthetic rate were all enhanced in EpTFIIAγ transgenic plants in all five wheat cultivars compared with their corresponding wild-type controls at all of the tillering, stem elongation, flowering and milk development stages under both full-irrigation and water-limited conditions (Fig. 2d–g and Supplementary Figs. 12–17). However, stomatal conductance and transpiration rate were lower in transgenic plants under water-limited conditions, although some EpTFIIAγ lines had slightly higher stomatal conductance under full-irrigation conditions. In agreement with these results, WUE (that is, the ratio of net photosynthetic rate to transpiration rate) was improved in EpTFIIAγ plants under water-limited conditions (Fig. 2d–g and Supplementary Figs. 14–17). Under full-irrigation field conditions, no obvious phenotypic changes in root development were seen between wild-type Fielder and transgenic plants. By contrast, all EpTFIIAγ lines had increased root length and biomass compared with Fielder under water-limited conditions (Fig. 2h–j), aligning with the stay-green phenotype observed in shoots (Supplementary Figs. 8 and 9). Together, field-grown EpTFIIAγ wheat lines have enhanced WUE, resulting in slower water consumption, delayed senescence under water-limited conditions, and consequently more extensive root development, thereby facilitating greater water uptake. These data also suggested that enhanced photosynthetic capacity and CO2 assimilation contributed to the increased biomass and grain yield observed in EpTFIIAγ wheat plants.

Industry observers note that eukaryotic transcription initiation by RNA polymerase II (Pol II) requires numerous general transcription factors and cofactors to nucleate at core promoter sites, which typically contain several DNA sequence elements (for example, TATA boxes), to form the pre-initiation complex27. Among them, the transcription initiation factor TFIIA is a general cofactor that acts as an anti-repressor or co-activator27,28. In multicellular eukaryotes, the TFIIA complex typically comprises α-subunit, β-subunit and γ-subunit, encoded by TFIIAαβ and TFIIAγ genes27,29. To characterize the function of EpTFIIAγ, we first examined TFIIAγ sequences across species. EpTFIIAγ retains a conserved protein architecture while also harbouring a unique, lineage-specific N-terminal extension (Supplementary Table 7 and Supplementary Fig. 18). To determine whether EpTFIIAγ participates in transcription initiation, we first examined its subcellular localization in wheat protoplasts. EpTFIIAγ–GFP mainly localized to the nucleus, whereas intact TaTFIIAγ–GFP and AtTFIIAγ–GFP fusions demonstrated both nuclear and cytoplasmic localization (Extended Data Fig. 6a,b). To investigate whether EpTFIIAγ could interact with endogenous TFIIAαβ to form the TFIIA holocomplex in plants, we conducted yeast two-hybrid, luciferase-complementation imaging and pulldown assays. These experiments consistently demonstrated that EpTFIIAγ fails to detectably interact with either wheat or Arabidopsis TFIIAαβ, whereas both TaTFIIAγ and AtTFIIAγ could interact with their corresponding TFIIAαβ proteins to form complete TFIIA complexes (Extended Data Fig. 6c–g). These results indicated that EpTFIIAγ does not appear to function as a transcription initiation factor in plants, or at least does so differently from these expression hosts.

The TFIIA recognition element (IIARE) located upstream of the TATA box enhances recruitment of TFIIA and other components to activate transcription at TATA-box promoter motifs27,29. We asked whether EpTFIIAγ could similarly bind to such recognition sites. Electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSAs) indicated that MBP–EpTFIIAγ could indeed directly bind to an IIARE-containing TATA box, whereas neither wheat TaTFIIAγ nor Arabidopsis AtTFIIAγ displayed detectable binding (Extended Data Fig. 6h,i). Although fungal and plant TFIIAγ proteins share conserved α-helical and β-sheet architectures, EpTFIIAγ uniquely harbours an N-terminal intrinsically disordered region (IDR; Fig. 3a). Hypothesizing that this region may confer specialized biological function, we generated an IDR deletion variant (EpTFIIAγ(ΔIDR)). This truncation did not bind to IIARE-containing TATA-box fragments, and likewise, its nuclear localization was impaired (Fig. 3b,c and Extended Data Fig. 6j). Conversely, fusing the EpTFIIAγ-derived IDR to TaTFIIAγ or AtTFIIAγ conferred binding to probes carrying an IIARE-containing TATA box (Fig. 3b and Extended Data Fig. 6j).

Data are mean ± s.d. from four biological replicates (j,k). Experiments were independently repeated three times with similar results (b,i). Statistical significance was determined by two-sided unpaired Student’s t-tests. **P < 0.01 indicates statistically significant differences. Gel source data are shown in Supplementary Fig. 25.

In a recent development, to test whether this IDR could drive liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS), we expressed EpTFIIAγ–GFP in Nicotiana benthamiana leaf epidermal cells. Upon hyperosmotic stress, EpTFIIAγ maintained a homogeneous nuclear distribution and did not coalesce into condensates under either stress or non-stress conditions (Supplementary Fig. 19a). Moreover, His–EpTFIIAγ did not detectably form dynamic droplets in vitro, indicating that its relatively short IDR was insufficient to trigger LLPS (Supplementary Fig. 19b). Further evaluation of chromatin-binding dynamics through fluorescence recovery after photobleaching and fluorescence correlation spectroscopy demonstrated that EpTFIIAγ(ΔIDR) exhibited markedly shallower bleach depth and accelerated recovery kinetics (Fig. 3c and Supplementary Fig. 19c–h), indicating attenuated chromatin association and higher mobility than full-length control. Stable-transgenic EpTFIIAγ(ΔIDR) expression in wheat cv. Fielder conferred no obvious improvement in drought resistance relative to wild-type (Extended Data Fig. 6k–m), indicating that the IDR is indeed indispensable for EpTFIIAγ function in the drought-stress response.

Recent findings suggest that to identify EpTFIIAγ-binding sites across the wheat genome, we performed chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by sequencing (ChIP–seq) with transgenic plants stably expressing EpTFIIAγ–HA in the cv. Fielder (Fig. 3d). Across two replicates, 17,131 putative EpTFIIAγ-binding sites were identified, 85% of which are in intergenic regions and 15% in genic regions, including gene bodies as well as the 3-kb upstream and 300-bp downstream flanking sequences presumed to harbour the promoter and transcriptional terminator, respectively (Fig. 3e). Analysis of 2,570 genic binding sites identified 1,347 annotated genes bound by EpTFIIAγ–HA (Fig. 3f and Supplementary Table 8), and the core motif within these binding regions was enriched with a TATA-containing element (Fig. 3g). Gene Ontology analysis found that these EpTFIIAγ–HA target genes were enriched in terms related to stress responses, such as ‘transcriptional regulation’, ‘response to water deprivation’, ‘response to osmotic stress’, ‘response to cold’, ‘regulation of stomatal movement’ and ‘transpiration’; hormone responses, such as ‘response to abscisic acid (ABA)’, ‘response to auxin’ and ‘response to brassinosteroid’, as well as ‘photosynthesis’ and ‘chlorophyll biosynthesis’ (Fig. 3h). Further EMSAs confirmed that EpTFIIAγ could bind to promoter regions of 387 wheat genes, underscoring its capacity to regulate diverse biological pathways in planta, such as those related to stress response, development, photosynthesis and yield formation (Extended Data Fig. 7a, Supplementary Table 9 and Supplementary Fig. 20).

Industry observers note that to define the regulatory network involved in the effects of EpTFIIAγ on photosynthetic efficiency, WUE and the drought-stress response, we compared transcriptomes of 20-day-old wild-type Fielder and EpTFIIAγ transgenic seedlings. This identified 1,953 differentially expressed genes (DEGs; fold change of more than 2 or less than 0.5, P < 0.05) in transgenic plants relative to Fielder, including 1,405 upregulated and 548 downregulated DEGs (Extended Data Fig. 7b–g and Supplementary Table 10). By examining overlap between ChIP–seq and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) datasets, we identified 1,056 candidate target genes that are potentially bound and transcriptionally regulated by EpTFIIAγ, including 824 upregulated and 232 downregulated genes in EpTFIIAγ plants (Extended Data Fig. 8a,b). Among them, stress-response-related genes involved in ABA and drought responses demonstrated strong enrichment (Extended Data Fig. 8c), such as wheat homologues of Arabidopsis MYBR1 (ref. 30), FBH4 (ref. 31) and DREB1C32 (Supplementary Tables 9 and 10). Other genes known to function in plant development, source–sink partitioning and grain yield were also present among upregulated DEGs, including the CONSTANS-like gene TaCol-B5 (ref. 33), wheat homologues of rice OsCIN2 (ref. 34) and OsSWEET4 (ref. 35), and homologues of Arabidopsis VND7 (ref. 36) and SWEET12 (ref. 37). Among photosynthesis-related DEGs, we found TaYCF9 and TaCP47, which are homologues of Arabidopsis PsbZ38 and CP47 (ref. 39) encoding subunits of the PSII reaction centre. In addition, we identified TaCOG1, a homologue of the Arabidopsis Dof transcription factor COG1, that promotes biomass accumulation by enhancing photosynthetic capacity40. TaGAPC1, a redox-dependent regulator of energy metabolism that mediates stress responses in Arabidopsis41, was also upregulated (Supplementary Tables 9 and 10).

MBP–EpTFIIAγ could bind in vitro to approximately 30-bp promoter fragments containing TATA motifs from TaDREB1C, TaFBH4, TaMYBR1, TaVND7, TaCol-B5, TaCIN2, TaSWEET4, TaSWEET12, TaYCF9, TaCP47, TaCOG1 and TaGAPC1, and this interaction could be compromised by competition from unlabelled probes (Fig. 3i, Extended Data Fig. 8d and Supplementary Fig. 21a). ChIP–quantitative PCR (qPCR) indicated that these promoter fragments highlighted greater enrichment in EpTFIIAγ–HA genomic DNA precipitated by anti-haemagglutinin antibody than by the immunoglobulin G (IgG) control (Fig. 3j and Extended Data Fig. 8e), demonstrating that EpTFIIAγ could indeed bind to TATA-containing core promoter motifs. In dual-luciferase reporter assays using approximately 1.5-kb promoter fragments, activities of target promoters were upregulated in the presence of EpTFIIAγ compared with empty vector controls (Fig. 3k, Extended Data Fig. 8f and Supplementary Fig. 21b), supported by real-time (RT)–qPCR analyses revealing that TaDREB1C, TaFBH4, TaMYBR1, TaVND7, TaCol-B5, TaCIN2, TaSWEET4, TaSWEET12, TaYCF9, TaCP47, TaCOG1 and TaGAPC1 mRNAs were all expressed at higher levels in all three EpTFIIAγ transgenic lines than in wild-type Fielder (Extended Data Fig. 8g). These results collectively indicated that EpTFIIAγ functions as a transcriptional cofactor to regulate target gene expression.

To determine how downstream regulatory targets contribute to enhancing drought resistance, photosynthetic efficiency and grain yield in EpTFIIAγ plants, we generated transgenic wheat lines overexpressing TaDREB1C, TaCOG1 or TaCIN2 in the cv. Fielder background. TaDREB1C lines had enhanced drought resistance and WUE through accelerated stomatal closure and reduced transpiration compared with Fielder under drought stress (Extended Data Fig. 9a–g). This overexpression did not detectably alter growth period, which remained comparable with controls under full irrigation (Extended Data Fig. 9h–j). Plants overexpressing TaCOG1 had enhanced photosynthetic and carbon-fixation capacities, resulting in increased biomass and grain yield relative to controls (Extended Data Fig. 9k–p). Moreover, TaCIN2 overexpression resulted in accelerated grain filling, ultimately increasing grain size and yield (Extended Data Fig. 9q–v). These results position the EpTFIIAγ regulon as pivotal for concurrently improving drought resilience and yield potential in wheat.

To investigate the mechanisms through which EpTFIIAγ drives enhanced drought resistance, photosynthetic capacity and grain yield, we conducted yeast two-hybrid screening using a cDNA library obtained from wheat cv. Chinese Spring seedlings. Four successive rounds of screening with EpTFIIAγ serving as bait yielded 112 candidate interacting proteins (Supplementary Table 11), including 22 putative transcription factors. After repeating yeast two-hybrid assays to confirm that EpTFIIAγ could interact with wheat homologues of Arabidopsis transcriptional activators WRKY46 (ref. 42), AKS1 (ref. 43), ARF6 (ref. 44) and VOZ1 (ref. 45) (Fig. 4a), luciferase-complementation imaging tested whether EpTFIIAγ could physically interact with these partners. Co-expression of EpTFIIAγ–C-terminal luciferase fragment (cLUC) with N-terminal luciferase fragment (nLUC)–TaWRKY46, nLUC–TaAKS1, nLUC–TaARF6 or nLUC–TaVOZ1 produced chemiluminescence, whereas no signal was observed in regions infiltrated with vector controls (Fig. 4b). Bimolecular fluorescence complementation assays further revealed that co-expression of the EpTFIIAγ–cYFP with nYFP–TaWRKY46, nYFP–TaAKS1, nYFP–TaARF6 or nYFP–TaVOZ1 led to obvious YFP signal (Fig. 4c and Supplementary Fig. 22a,b). Pulldown assays indicated that MBP–EpTFIIAγ could interact with GST–TaWRKY46, GST–TaAKS1, GST–TaARF6 and HA–TaVOZ1 in vitro (Fig. 4d). Co-immunoprecipitation assays in N. benthamiana leaves co-expressing 35Spro:GFP–EpTFIIAγ and 35Spro:mCherry–TaWRKY46, 35Spro:mCherry–TaARF6 or 35Spro:mCherry–EpTFIIAγ with 35Spro:GFP–TaAKS1, 35Spro:GFP–TaVOZ1 also confirmed that EpTFIIAγ could physically interact with these transcription factors in planta (Fig. 4e). By contrast, the IDR-deleted EpTFIIAγ variant failed to detectably interact with any tested partners (Supplementary Fig. 22c,d), highlighting the essential role of this IDR. Moreover, no interactions were observed between wheat TaTFIIAγ and the transcription factors TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 or TaVOZ1 (Supplementary Fig. 22e,f), underscoring EpTFIIAγ functional specificity.

To map genome-wide binding sites and target genes, we used CUT&Tag in stable-transgenic cv. Fielder plants expressing TaWRKY46–HA, TaAKS1–FLAG, TaARF6–HA or TaVOZ1–HA. Integrative analysis identified 467, 309, 495 and 505 target genes that are potentially co-bound and co-regulated by EpTFIIAγ with TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 or TaVOZ1, respectively (Supplementary Table 12 and Supplementary Fig. 23), suggesting direct involvement in the EpTFIIAγ regulatory network. GST–TaWRKY46 could bind in vitro to probes containing the W-box from the TaCol-B5, TaSWEET4 and TaSWEET12 promoters, and these binding events increased in the presence of MBP–EpTFIIAγ (Fig. 4f and Extended Data Fig. 10a). Similarly, GST–TaAKS1 could bind to probes harbouring the G-box or E-box from the TaDREB1C, TaCol-B5, TaYCF9 or TaCOG1 promoter regions, with the addition of MBP–EpTFIIAγ markedly strengthening these interactions in vitro. Moreover, GST–TaARF6 could interact with AuxRE-containing probes derived from the TaYCF9, TaFBH4 and TaCIN2 promoters, which was boosted by addition of MBP–EpTFIIAγ, whereas GST–TaVOZ1 bound to probes with a 5′-CTTCTT-3′ motif present in the TaCP47, TaVND7, TaMYBR1 and TaGAPC1 promoter regions, which also increased in the presence of MBP–EpTFIIAγ (Fig. 4f and Extended Data Fig. 10a). Dual-luciferase reporter assays indicated that TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1 could activate genes with corresponding promoter recognition sites (Fig. 4g and Extended Data Fig. 10b).

To determine whether EpTFIIAγ functions coordinately with or independently of TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1 in regulating target genes, we performed dual-luciferase reporter assays. Upon co-expressing EpTFIIAγ with each respective transcription factor, LUC activity driven by the TaDREB1C, TaFBH4, TaMYBR1, TaVND7, TaCol-B5, TaCIN2, TaSWEET4, TaSWEET12, TaYCF9, TaCP47, TaCOG1 and TaGAPC1 promoters was greater than the expression of wheat transcription factors alone (Fig. 4g and Extended Data Fig. 10b). To clarify whether activation of these transcription-factor genes contributed to the observed drought resistance of transgenic EpTFIIAγ plants, we examined drought resistance in lines overexpressing TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1 (Extended Data Fig. 11a–d), as well as wrky46-knockout and arf6-knockout mutants by gene editing in cv. Fielder (Extended Data Fig. 11e,f). All overexpression lines had enhanced drought resistance relative to Fielder, whereas both mutants had compromised drought resistance compared with Fielder controls (Extended Data Fig. 11g–j). To further characterize the genetic interactions of EpTFIIAγ with TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1, we crossed EpTFIIAγ plants (Fielder background) with each overexpression line. Under normal conditions, homozygous double-transgene-positive progeny of all crosses bore phenotypes comparable with that of TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1 overexpression plants. By contrast, double-transgene-carrying hybrids highlighted stronger drought resistance than control plants expressing a single transgene (Extended Data Fig. 11k,l). These findings collectively demonstrated that EpTFIIAγ physically interacts with select transcription activators, such as TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 or TaVOZ1, and that their interactions resulted in additive effects on EpTFIIAγ target gene expression, consequently enhancing the drought response, photosynthesis and grain yield.

According to recent reports, to determine whether EpTFIIAγ function in conferring drought resistance was conserved in other major cereal crops, we generated three transgenic EpTFIIAγ lines each in rice cv. Nipponbare and maize inbred line B73 backgrounds (Fig. 5a,b). In greenhouse drought-resistance assays, survival of transgenic EpTFIIAγ rice and maize lines was extended by approximately 2.6-fold and approximately 2.8-fold for rice (Fig. 5c,d) and maize (Fig. 5e,f), respectively, compared with their wild-type controls. Transcriptomic analysis found that genes involved in ‘transcriptional regulation’, ‘response to ABA’, ‘response to water deprivation’, ‘response to osmotic stress’ and ‘photosynthesis’ were enriched among upregulated DEGs in EpTFIIAγ seedlings of both species (Extended Data Fig. 12a,b and Supplementary Tables 13 and 14).
